TITLE: The Association of African Universities Appoints a New Secretary General – Professor Olusola Bandele Oyewole

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
For Immediate Release

PRESS RELEASE

Accra, Ghana (9th August 2021) – The outgoing President of the AAU Governing Board, Professor Orlando Antonio Quilambo (Rector of Eduardo Mondlane University, Mozambique), has announced the appointment of a new Secretary General for the Association of African Universities effective 1st October 2021. Following a highly competitive recruitment process, Professor Olusola Bandele Oyewole was chosen to take over the running of the 54-year-old Association. He will replace the very able Professor Etienne Ehouan Ehile, an Ivorian higher education leader, who has led the Association for the past nine (9) years.

Professor Olusola Bandele Oyewole is a Nigerian professor of Food Science and Technology, specifically Food Microbiology and Biotechnology. He is not new to the Association because he has been a staff member of the Association in the past, as well as a Board Member and President of the Association. He is the former Vice Chancellor of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Nigeria and has also worked as a Senior Expert in Higher Education for the African Union Commission in Ethiopia. Professor Oyewole’s work experiences at the national, regional and continental levels have endowed him with a wealth of knowledge in coordinating multinational research and development programs. He therefore comes to the AAU fully equipped for the job ahead of him.

In his acceptance remarks today, 9th August 2021, during the virtual extra-ordinary general conference organized by the Association, he paid tribute to the out-going Secretary General Professor Etienne Ehouan Ehile, saying that he was aware that he had “big shoes to fill”. He recognized Prof Ehile’s sterling work that saw the Association increasing its visibility, decentralizing its functions through regional offices, diversifying the capacity building initiatives, identifying new partners, nurturing the relationship with the government of Ghana and continuing the advocacy to various stakeholders to support higher education in Africa. Professor Oyewole thanked the AAU Governing Board for the opportunity given to him to serve the Association.

“My vision is to amplify the relevance of the Association of African Universities as the Voice of Higher Education in Africa” said Professor Oyewole in his acceptance remarks. He revealed that during his term of office, his top focus areas will include identifying and implementing strategies for sustaining the Association during and post the COVID19 era and helping African Universities to overcome the challenges of COVID19.

Professor Oyewole said that he deems the strategic collaborations and dialogues with development partners and other stakeholders as key for the successful future of the Association. “Without strong partnerships and collaborations, the Association would be unable to achieve her grand mission of improving the quality of African Higher Education. Through honest, sincere, visionary, committed, transparent and disciplined leadership, I intend to build new strategic partnerships and revive old partnerships for the sustainability of the Association”, he added. Through vibrant platforms for learning and knowledge exchange, Professor Olusola Bandele Oyewole envisions the building of the next generation of academics in Africa, stronger intellectual engagement and the full engagement of AAU Member Universities – and African Universities in general.

For the full profile of Professor Oyewole feel free to download his curriculum vitae from here: https://blog.aau.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/New-SG-Prof.-Olusola-Oyewole-CV.pdf

– END –

About the Association of African Universities, AAU (https://www.aau.org/)

The Association of African Universities is an international non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African Universities to promote cooperation among them on the one hand, and between them and the international academic community on the other. Created in 1967, the AAU is the voice of higher education in Africa. AAU aims to improve the quality of African higher education, and to strengthen its contribution to Africa’s development by supporting the core functions of higher education institutions and facilitating critical reflection and consensus building on issues affecting higher education. It is headquartered in Accra, Ghana, has a membership of more than 400 HEIs and has three regional offices – North Africa Regional Office (NARO) in Cairo, Egypt; East Africa Regional Office (EARO) in Khartoum, Sudan; and North America Office (NAMO) in Washington DC, USA. The Association is the technical implementing arm of the African Union in higher education – with coverage and mandate across the language divide of Africa. We have influence in the francophone, anglophone, lusophone and arabophone regions. The AAU is the coordinating agency of the Higher Education Cluster of the Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA 16-25) of the African Union Commission (AUC). Through our guidance, our member universities are responsible for implementing the Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy for Africa (STISA 2024) of the AUC

TITLE: AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants 2026: Up to €3,000 for Doctoral Researchers in Sub-Saharan Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 are now open to eligible doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa seeking financial support to undertake a short research stay at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country.

Supported by the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (AvH), the programme is designed to strengthen scientific capacity, research collaboration, networking, and knowledge exchange among young researchers across sub-Saharan Africa.

The grants enable eligible doctoral candidates to spend one to two months at a host university or research institution in another sub-Saharan African country while working with an experienced scientific host. The research stay must contribute directly to the applicant’s doctoral research.

For the 2026 call, applications must be submitted in English by 16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT.

What Are the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants?

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants are research mobility opportunities designed to support junior researchers pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa.

The programme allows doctoral candidates to temporarily move to another sub-Saharan African country to undertake research activities that cannot be conducted in their home country.

During the research stay, the researcher works with an identified scientific host at a university or research institute.

The programme aims to strengthen:

Scientific research capacity

Research collaboration between African institutions

Professional networks among young researchers

International scientific networking

Knowledge and skills transfer

Collaboration between doctoral researchers and experienced researchers

Research that contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries

The programme is supported financially by BMZ and with support from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation.

Two AGNES Mobility Grant Programmes

The 2026 call provides two different mobility grant opportunities.

1. General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant

The General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is generally open to both male and female candidates.

Eligible male and female doctoral researchers can apply for this grant provided they meet the programme requirements.

2. Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant

The Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is specifically for female candidates.

Female researchers may apply for either the General Grant, the Special Grant, or both.

However, a female applicant can receive a maximum of one grant.

Male candidates are only eligible to apply for the General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant.

AGNES also encourages applications from researchers across a wide range of disciplines, including:

Sciences

Humanities

Law

Social Sciences

No Geographical Quota

The 2026 call states that there is no geographical quota for AGNES grants within sub-Saharan Africa.

This means eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply.

However, AGNES specifically welcomes applications from eligible candidates from countries described in the call as under-represented.

These include:

Burkina Faso

Ghana

Guinea

Côte d’Ivoire

Liberia

Mali

Senegal

Sierra Leone

Angola

Central African Republic

Chad

Congo Brazzaville

Democratic Republic of the Congo

Equatorial Guinea

Gabon

Rwanda

Zambia

Uganda

Tanzania

Malawi

Lesotho

Botswana

Mozambique

Mauritius

Mauritania

Namibia

Zimbabwe

Cape Verde

Sao Tome and Principe

Importantly, being from one of these countries is not presented as an exclusive eligibility requirement. The call states that all eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply.

What Does the Grant Support?

The AGNES Mobility Grant enables a doctoral researcher to undertake a research stay lasting between one and two months at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country.

The proposed research must form part of the applicant’s doctoral research.

Eligible activities may include:

Laboratory research

Bench work

Research studies

Library research

Data or other research activities

Writing part of the doctoral thesis

Other activities directly related to the doctoral research

The proposed research should contribute meaningfully to the applicant’s doctoral work.

The applicant must also demonstrate why the research is relevant to the further development of their home country or other sub-Saharan African countries.

Research Must Not Be Possible in the Home Country

One of the important conditions is that the proposed research activity cannot be conducted in the applicant’s home country.

Applicants therefore need to demonstrate why the host institution provides research facilities, expertise, resources, or other conditions that are unavailable in the applicant’s home country.

This is an important consideration when preparing the research proposal.

Financial Support

The AGNES grant is intended to be financially comprehensive for the short research stay as far as reasonably possible.

The grant can support expenses associated with:

Travel

Subsistence

Research-related expenses

Host institution research costs, where applicable

The maximum grant depends on the length of the research stay.

Maximum Grant Amounts

Research Stay
Maximum Grant

1 month
€2,300

1.5 months
€2,650

2 months
€3,000

These amounts represent the maximum overall budget, including the host fee.

Research Allowance for the Host Institution

A portion of the grant may be allocated to research costs at the host institution.

The call specifies the following deductions from the total grant:

Humanities and Social Sciences: €100 per month

Natural and Life Sciences and Engineering Sciences: €200 per month

The scientific host and host institution must request the relevant research cost allowance as part of the required documentation.

Travel Support

Applicants must provide two travel quotations for their journey.

The quotes should cover return travel between:

The applicant’s country of residence; and

The country where the host institution is located.

Travel may be by:

Land transportation; or

Economy-class flight

Applicants should therefore research the expected cost of their return journey before submitting the application.

Cost of Living

Applicants must also provide an estimate of their expected cost of living during the research stay.

This should take into account expenses such as:

Accommodation or rent

Meals

Local transportation

Health insurance

Applicants are expected to obtain valid health insurance for the duration of their research stay.

The scientific host and host institution are expected to assist applicants in finding affordable accommodation and preparing realistic subsistence estimates.

APPLY HERE

Who Can Apply?

The programme is specifically aimed at junior researchers who are currently pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa.

Applicants must meet several eligibility requirements.

1. Must Be a Doctoral Student

The applicant must be officially registered for a doctoral degree at a university or tertiary institution in sub-Saharan Africa at the time of application.

Current doctoral students are eligible.

The call specifically states that applicants must provide official proof of registration for their postgraduate degree.

2. Must Be a National of a Sub-Saharan African Country

Applicants must be nationals of a sub-Saharan African country.

The programme therefore focuses specifically on researchers from sub-Saharan Africa.

3. Must Have at Least One Published Research Article

Applicants must have at least one published article from their thesis work.

The article must have been published in a non-predatory journal.

The call specifies that only journals indexed by:

SCOPUS, or

Web of Science

will be considered.

Applicants therefore need to provide evidence that their publication meets these requirements.

4. Research Must Be Relevant to Development

The applicant must clearly demonstrate how their research contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries.

The proposal should therefore explain the broader relevance and potential development contribution of the research.

5. Research Must Require the Host Institution

The applicant must demonstrate that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country.

This requirement helps ensure that the mobility component of the grant is necessary for the proposed research.

6. Identified Scientific Host Required

Applicants must already have an identified scientific host.

The applicant and scientific host must agree on:

The research proposal

The research activities

The work schedule

The timing of the research stay

Applications without an identified scientific host and mutually agreed proposal/work schedule will not be considered.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit a complete application containing all required documents.

The maximum total application size is 12 MB.

1. Research or Project Proposal

Applicants must prepare a short research/project proposal.

The proposal:

Must be written in English.

Must not exceed five pages.

Must outline the proposed research activity.

Must explain the research objectives.

Must include a work schedule.

Must explain how the research will be undertaken at the host institution.

The scientific host must agree in writing to the proposal and proposed schedule.

2. Standard CV

Applicants must submit a standard CV using the AGNES CV template.

The CV must be written in English.

The official 2026 AGNES Mobility CV template is provided as part of the application information.

3. Proof of Doctoral Registration

Applicants must provide official proof that they are currently registered for their doctoral degree.

This is an important requirement because the programme is specifically intended for current doctoral students.

4. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit official academic transcripts showing grades obtained during:

Undergraduate studies

Postgraduate studies, where applicable

If the transcript is written in a language other than English, applicants must also provide an official explanation of the grading system in English.

5. List of Publications

Applicants must provide a list of their published articles in eligible non-predatory journals.

The publication list must include SCOPUS or Web of Science links for each publication.

Applicants must also include an electronic copy of the first page of each publication showing:

Article title

Authors

Abstract

The publication list and first pages of the publications must be combined into one PDF document.

The document should begin with a descriptive title, such as:

“LIST OF PUBLICATIONS FOR [APPLICANT’S NAME]”

The publication list should then be followed by the first page of each publication.

6. Travel Quotations

Applicants must provide two travel quotations for return travel between their country of residence and the host institution’s country.

The quotes can cover:

Land travel; or

Economy-class air travel

7. Estimated Cost of Living

Applicants must provide an estimated budget for their stay.

The estimate should cover:

Rent/accommodation

Meals

Local transportation

Health insurance

8. Letter of Invitation From the Scientific Host

The scientific host must provide a letter of invitation written in English.

The letter must:

Confirm that a place to work will be available during the proposed research period.

Include a binding declaration from the host institution requesting the relevant research cost allowance.

The host institution should therefore be involved in the preparation of the application rather than being contacted only after the application is submitted.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants 2026

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted online using the application form provided by AGNES.

The application form is:

https://forms.gle/t57E7k9gTTtd7R7XA

Applicants should carefully check their application before submitting it.

The call specifically warns that applications that:

Do not follow the stated guidelines; or

Are missing required documents

will be automatically rejected.

Applicants should therefore make sure that all required documents are complete, correctly formatted, written in the required language, and included before submission.

Application Language

All applications must be submitted in English.

This applies particularly to the research proposal, CV, scientific host invitation letter, and other documents where English is specifically required.

Applicants whose academic transcripts use another language must provide the required official explanation of the grading system in English.

Grant Acceptance and Reporting Requirements

The grant is a once-off award and cannot be used to finance research stays retrospectively.

If selected, both the grant recipient and the scientific host must provide:

A signed letter of acceptance

A contractual agreement

These documents must be emailed to the AGNES Governing Board within two weeks of receiving the offer, according to the call information.

Following completion of the research stay, both the grantee and scientific host are expected to report to AGNES on the progress and success of their collaboration.

This report is expected within six months after completion of the research stay.

Research Stay Timeline

The selection meeting is scheduled for December 2026.

Only selected candidates will be notified.

The earliest possible start date for research stays is:

1 March 2027

Research stays must be completed by:

31 July 2027

Applicants should therefore consider these dates when discussing the proposed research schedule with their scientific host.

Important Dates

Stage
Date

Application deadline
16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT

Selection meeting
December 2026

Earliest research stay commencement
1 March 2027

Latest completion of research stay
31 July 2027

Key Points Applicants Should Understand

Before applying, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the following requirements:

You must currently be registered for a doctoral degree.

You must be a national of a sub-Saharan African country.

You must have at least one thesis-related article published in an eligible journal.

The journal must be indexed by SCOPUS or Web of Science.

You must identify a scientific host in another sub-Saharan African country.

Your host must agree to your proposal and work schedule.

The proposed research must contribute to your doctoral research.

The research must be relevant to development in sub-Saharan Africa.

The research activity must not be possible in your home country.

Your proposal must be written in English and must not exceed five pages.

Your CV must use the AGNES template.

You must provide academic transcripts.

You must provide evidence of your eligible publications.

You must provide two travel quotations.

You must provide an estimated cost of living.

You must provide a scientific host invitation letter.

The complete application must be submitted online before the deadline.

Missing documents or failure to follow the guidelines can result in automatic rejection.

Why the Programme Matters

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is structured around more than simply providing funding for a short research trip.

The programme aims to strengthen research connections within Africa by allowing doctoral researchers to work with institutions and experienced researchers in other sub-Saharan African countries.

This creates opportunities for researchers to gain access to expertise, facilities, research environments, and professional networks that may not be available at their home institutions.

The programme also places emphasis on research that can contribute to the development of sub-Saharan African countries, meaning applicants are expected to demonstrate the wider relevance of their doctoral research.

The involvement of scientific hosts also creates an opportunity for longer-term professional and research collaboration.

Conclusion

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 provide doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa with an opportunity to undertake a one- to two-month research stay at another African university or research institution.

With grants of up to €3,000, the programme can contribute toward travel, subsistence, and research-related costs while giving researchers an opportunity to collaborate with experienced scientists and strengthen their professional networks.

The programme is open across academic disciplines, including Sciences, Humanities, Law, and Social Sciences, while the Special AGNES Mobility Grant provides an additional application route specifically for female researchers.

However, applicants must meet several specific requirements, particularly being current doctoral students, having at least one eligible published thesis-related article, identifying a scientific host, and demonstrating that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country.

Interested researchers should begin preparing their research proposal, publication evidence, host invitation, travel quotations, transcripts, and other required documents well before the deadline.

This new partnership is fully aligned with ESF’s Strategy 2024-2028, which lines of action places a strong emphasis on:

Connecting research communities, disciplines, stakeholder groups, and geographies

Implementing the full spectrum of science management services

Promoting excellence and inclusion in European research

Together with AERG, we are committed to building bridges across the scientific community and strengthening the voice of researchers in shaping Europe’s research agenda.

ESF fosters cooperation in research and science policy through a wide network of institutional partnerships. With over 80 active collaborations through hosted platforms, coordinated projects and service provision agreements, ESF continues to expand its reach and impact across Europe.

Artificial intelligence governance

Technology regulation

Digital rights

The relationship between state power and corporate power

Technology’s impact on democracy and society

Other pressing technology policy questions

What the 2027 Fellowship Offers

One of the major benefits of the program is the financial support provided to each selected fellow.

$10,000 Fellowship Stipend

Each fellow will receive a $10,000 stipend to support their work during the fellowship.

The stipend will be distributed quarterly, allowing fellows to receive financial support throughout the year as they work on their projects.

Editorial Guidance

Fellows will receive ongoing editorial guidance from the Tech Policy Press team. This support is intended to help fellows strengthen their reporting, analysis and overall body of work.

International Fellowship Cohort

Selected fellows will become part of an international cohort of current fellows who can exchange ideas, provide feedback and collaborate where appropriate.

This creates an opportunity to build relationships with professionals working on technology policy and related issues in different countries and regions.

Monthly Learning and Exchange Sessions

Fellows will participate in monthly sessions designed to support and strengthen their work. These sessions provide opportunities for learning, discussion, feedback and the exchange of ideas.

Opportunity to Build a Significant Body of Work

Over the course of the 12-month fellowship, participants will have the opportunity to develop a substantial body of reporting and analysis around an important technology policy issue.

The fellowship can therefore provide a structured environment for professionals who want to deepen their expertise and produce high-quality public-interest work.

Visibility Through Tech Policy Press

Tech Policy Press plans to publish fellows’ work on its website and feature it prominently in its newsletter.

Fellowship projects may also be highlighted through:

The Tech Policy Press podcast

Special events

Other opportunities to showcase fellows’ work

This can provide fellows with an opportunity to reach both the general public and decision-makers interested in technology policy.

Areas of Work for Fellows

Applicants are expected to have a clear area of focus and explain how their proposed work can contribute to public understanding and decision-making.

The fellowship welcomes work related to a wide range of technology policy topics.

Potential areas may include:

Artificial intelligence governance

Technology regulation

Digital rights

Technology and democracy

Technology and society

Digital governance

State and corporate power

Technology policy in particular countries or regions

Underreported technology policy issues

The impact of technology on communities

Other issues that fall within Tech Policy Press’s editorial focus

Applicants do not necessarily have to restrict themselves to one specific topic throughout the entire fellowship. The program encourages fellows to respond to relevant news and developments as they relate to their area of expertise.

Focus on Underrepresented Communities and Regions

Tech Policy Press is particularly interested in projects that center communities and regions that are often left out of global technology policy conversations.

This makes the fellowship especially relevant for applicants who can bring perspectives, expertise or reporting from areas that are not adequately represented in mainstream technology policy discussions.

There is no specific preferred geographic or thematic focus for applicants from the Global South, according to the fellowship’s frequently asked questions.

Fellowship Responsibilities and Expectations

Successful fellows will have a number of responsibilities throughout the 12-month program.

1. Produce Regular Reporting or Analysis

Fellows will be expected to contribute reporting or analysis related to technology and democracy at least once per month.

Although topics may evolve after the fellowship begins, applicants should clearly explain:

The topic they intend to focus on

Why the issue is important

Why they are well positioned to cover it

How their work will contribute to public understanding and decision-making

2. Attend Monthly Cohort Meetings

Fellows must attend a mandatory one-hour monthly cohort meeting.

These meetings provide an opportunity for fellows to connect with one another and participate in the fellowship’s collaborative learning environment.

3. Attend Monthly Editorial Check-Ins

Fellows will also participate in monthly meetings with the Tech Policy Press editorial team.

These meetings will be used to:

Review progress

Discuss challenges

Evaluate upcoming work

Determine next steps

4. Collaborate With Other Fellows

Fellows may be expected to collaborate with other members of the fellowship cohort and the Tech Policy Press masthead when appropriate.

5. Meet Agreed Deadlines

Participants must meet all deadlines agreed upon with the Tech Policy Press team for their work and other fellowship outputs.

6. Disclose Conflicts of Interest

Fellows are expected to disclose any potential conflicts of interest connected to their work.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship welcomes applications from professionals including:

Journalists

Researchers

Lawyers

Public policy professionals

APPLY HERE

Applicants should have a demonstrated interest or background in technology policy, media or a related field and be committed to producing high-quality public-interest work during the fellowship.

Applicants should also be able to demonstrate strong expertise in a particular technology policy issue, geography or broader area involving technology’s impact on democracy or society.

Tech Policy Press encourages applications from the Global Majority and communities that are underrepresented in media.

International Applicants Are Welcome

The 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship is open to applicants internationally.

The organization specifically confirms that international applicants are encouraged to apply and that the fellowship is open to candidates from around the world.

Applicants outside the United States do not need to be authorized to work in the United States to participate in the fellowship.

All fellows will work remotely as independent contractors.

What Counts as Published Work?

Applicants are required to provide links to previous publications.

A qualifying published work should:

Be publicly accessible online

Clearly identify the applicant as the author or contributor

Represent work that has actually been published

Examples of acceptable published work include:

Reported articles

Policy analyses

Issue analyses

Opinion articles

Essays

Podcasts

Newsletters

Data projects

However, social media posts are not considered published work for this application.

Unpublished materials such as class assignments and dissertations are also not accepted.

Applicants who submit translated work may do so, but they must provide at least one submission written in English. Applicants are also expected to demonstrate their own command of English.

If a submitted article is behind a paywall, applicants must ensure that the pieces submitted for consideration are open access.

How Recent Should Your Writing Samples Be?

Writing samples should generally be from the past three years.

Applicants should therefore prioritize recent work that demonstrates their current expertise, writing ability and understanding of their chosen technology policy area.

Can Applicants Submit Co-Authored Work?

Yes. Co-authored publications are permitted.

However, Tech Policy Press recommends that applicants submit at least one solo publication as part of their application.

This gives the selection team an opportunity to assess the applicant’s individual writing and analytical capabilities.

Can Fellows Work Across Multiple Formats?

Yes.

Applicants will not be disadvantaged for being open to working in multiple formats. The fellowship welcomes contributions across different forms of public-interest journalism, analysis and related work, provided that the work aligns with Tech Policy Press’s editorial focus.

Fellowship Application Requirements

Applicants must submit an online application containing the required supporting materials.

The application requires:

Curriculum vitae or resume

Cover letter of no more than two pages

Links to previous publications

Two professional references

What Should the Cover Letter Include?

The cover letter should explain what the applicant hopes to accomplish during the fellowship.

Applicants should use the cover letter to clearly communicate their proposed area of focus and demonstrate why they are well positioned to pursue the work.

A strong application should make it clear what issue the applicant wants to explore and how their work could contribute to public understanding and informed decision-making.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship is:

September 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

Applicants should complete and submit the online application before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the official Tech Policy Press application form.

Applicants should prepare their resume or CV, cover letter, publication links and two professional references before beginning the application.

Application: https://airtable.com/appfRgsTRubbZBBPq/pagINFzaysYPJ2qJ3/form

Information Sessions for Applicants

Tech Policy Press will host two online information sessions for people considering applying.

Registration is required.

Information Session 1

Date: September 9, 2026

Time: 8:00 a.m. EDT

Platform: Zoom

Information Session 2

Date: September 16, 2026

Time: 7:00 p.m. EDT

Platform: Zoom

Applicants can choose whichever session is more convenient.

The sessions provide an opportunity for potential applicants to learn more about the fellowship before submitting their applications.

Visit HERE to learn more about the 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship

When Will Selected Fellows Be Notified?

Tech Policy Press aims to notify applicants about their application status by early December 2026.

A selected pool of applicants may also be invited to participate in an online interview as part of the selection process.

When Does the Fellowship Begin?

The 2027 fellowship is scheduled to begin in January 2027.

The program will run for 12 months, meaning the fellowship will continue throughout 2027.

The fellowship is part-time, allowing participants to continue engaging with their professional work while contributing to their fellowship responsibilities.

Are Monthly Submissions Exclusive?

Yes.

Monthly submissions are expected to be exclusive to Tech Policy Press, although fellows may republish their work afterward.

This arrangement allows Tech Policy Press to publish and showcase fellows’ work while still giving fellows the ability to distribute their work more broadly after publication.

How Tech Policy Press Supports Fellows’ Work

Beyond the stipend and editorial guidance, the program provides an environment designed to help fellows develop their work and professional networks.

Participants can benefit from:

An international network of current and past fellows

Regular feedback and exchange of ideas

Editorial support

Monthly learning opportunities

Opportunities to develop sources within their focus area

Publication opportunities through Tech Policy Press

Potential exposure through the organization’s newsletter

Potential podcast and event opportunities

A structured year-long environment for producing public-interest work

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Technology Policy Professionals

Technology is increasingly connected to questions surrounding democracy, governance, rights, public policy and society. This fellowship provides an opportunity for experienced professionals to dedicate a year to examining these issues through reporting and analysis.

The combination of a $10,000 stipend, editorial support, international networking, publication opportunities and a structured 12-month program makes the fellowship particularly relevant to professionals looking to expand their body of work in technology policy.

It can also provide a platform for people who want to bring greater attention to technology policy issues affecting communities and regions that are often underrepresented in global discussions.

Conclusion

The 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship offers journalists, researchers, lawyers and public policy professionals an opportunity to spend a year developing independent reporting and analysis on important questions surrounding technology and democracy.

Selected fellows will receive a $10,000 stipend, participate in an international cohort, receive ongoing editorial guidance and have opportunities to publish and showcase their work through Tech Policy Press.

The fellowship is part-time, remote and open to applicants worldwide, making it accessible to professionals both inside and outside the United States.

Those interested in applying should begin preparing their CV or resume, two-page cover letter, recent published work and two professional references well before the deadline.

Application deadline: September 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

TITLE: eLearning Summit 2025: Strengthening Digital Education in Africa Through Quality, Collaboration, and Workforce Development

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Press Release – Accra, Ghana (March 19, 2025) – The Association of African Universities (AAU), in collaboration with eLearnAfrica, is excited to announce the eLearning Summit 2025, scheduled to take place virtually on April 17, 2025, at 1 PM GMT / 3 PM SAST. Click to register here: https://forms.gle/W6VwJ3GFNoyWQenx8

The summit will bring together higher education leaders, policymakers, instructional designers, edtech innovators, and industry experts to explore strategies for expanding digital learning opportunities across Africa under the theme “Transforming Online Learning in Africa: Scaling Quality, Partnerships, and Workforce Development through Digital Education“.

Following the success of the inaugural eLearning Summit in 2024, this edition will focus on enhancing the quality of online programmes, fostering impactful partnerships, and aligning digital education with Africa’s workforce development needs.

Launch Event on AAU Talks

As part of the build-up to the summit, the event will be launched on AAU Talks on AAUTV on Thursday, 20th March 2025, at 1 PM GMT / 2 PM SAST. The launch will provide deeper insights into key issues surrounding e-learning in Africa and set the stage for discussions leading up to the main event.

What to Expect

The eLearning Summit 2025 will feature high-level discussions, expert insights, and practical solutions aimed at strengthening Africa’s digital education landscape. Participants can expect engaging keynote addresses, thought-provoking panel discussions, and case study presentations from leading universities and industry experts.

One of the summit’s highlights will be case studies showcasing successful implementations of online MBA programs and professional development courses. Universities that have effectively developed and scaled their online programs, increased student enrollments, and enhanced digital learning infrastructure will share their experiences. These presentations and panel discussions will offer valuable insights into best practices, challenges faced, and strategies for ensuring sustainability in online education.

This free virtual summit is open to educators, administrators, policymakers, and all stakeholders committed to advancing online education in Africa. Attendees will have the opportunity to learn from thought leaders, discover innovative solutions for improving online learning quality and accessibility, explore partnership opportunities to enhance institutional capabilities, and gain insights into workforce needs and how digital education can bridge the skills gap. Click to register here: https://forms.gle/W6VwJ3GFNoyWQenx8

In 2016, eLearnAfrica entered into a partnership with the Association of African Universities (AAU), the largest higher education coordinating body in Africa, representing over 430 member universities across the continent. This collaboration aims to provide online, distance-learning opportunities to over 10 million African students, supporting universities in expanding their reach.

The partnership has made significant strides, now boasting over 140 registered users(universities, institutions, as well as individual professors and course holders). TITLE: Up to 3 PhD Scholarships in Germany with €1,650 Monthly Stipend at the University of Vechta

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The University of Vechta in Germany is inviting applications for up to three PhD scholarships within the doctoral college “Justice Dimensions of Sustainability-Oriented Transformation Processes in Rural Areas” (PK 060).

Funded by the Hans Böckler Foundation, the doctoral college focuses on understanding the social justice challenges associated with sustainability-oriented transformation processes, with particular attention to rural areas.

The programme brings together research on sustainability, social justice, rural development, environmental change, technological transformation and other related areas. It welcomes researchers from several academic disciplines and supports both qualitative and quantitative research approaches, with quantitative and mixed-methods research explicitly encouraged.

The scholarships are expected to begin between June and September 2027 and can be awarded for a maximum of three years.

The application deadline is November 2, 2026.

About the Doctoral College

The doctoral college is affiliated with the Vechta Institute of Sustainability Transformation in Rural Areas (VISTRA) at the University of Vechta.

Sustainability transformation has become an important subject of scientific, political and social discussion. However, major transformation processes can have different consequences for different groups within society.

While some people may benefit from new technologies, policies and economic opportunities, others may experience negative consequences or what the programme describes as “transformation pains.”

These differences raise important questions about social justice.

The doctoral college seeks to address these questions by investigating how sustainability-oriented transformations affect people and communities and how transformation processes can be designed in ways that are considered fair and socially just.

Particular attention is given to rural areas, where sustainability transformations can have distinctive economic, social, environmental and technological consequences.

The programme aims to make a significant contribution to research in this area through a comparative case study approach across individual doctoral projects.

Research Areas and Possible PhD Topics

The doctoral college provides several examples of research topics that could be explored through doctoral projects. These examples are not intended to represent an exhaustive list.

Transformation of the Energy Sector

Research could examine issues surrounding energy affordability and the emergence of new forms of inequality between urban and rural areas.

Potential areas of investigation include the distribution of costs and benefits associated with energy transitions and how changes in the energy sector affect different communities.

Spatial Justice

Applicants may explore questions related to fairness and equality across geographical spaces.

Possible topics include:

Equitable livelihoods

Social places

Local resilience

Rural and urban inequalities

Access to opportunities and resources

Normative Uncertainty

Another possible area of research concerns uncertainty about what constitutes the appropriate ethical standard for designing just sustainability transformations.

This could involve examining the theoretical and practical difficulties involved in determining what a fair transformation should look like.

Risk, Uncertainty and Perceived Justice

Research may also examine how risk and uncertainty influence people’s perceptions of justice and injustice during transformation processes.

Socio-Technical Transitions and Innovation

The doctoral college is interested in justice-related questions arising from technological and innovation processes.

Potential examples include:

Digitalisation

Bio-economy

Socio-technical transitions

Innovation processes

Technological change in rural areas

Nature and Climate Protection Policies

Applicants may investigate the justice-related consequences of policies designed to protect nature and address climate change.

Research could consider issues such as:

Urban-rural relationships

Climate protection policies

Nature conservation

Relationships between the Global North and Global South

Gender Justice

Another potential area is the role of gender justice in the design and implementation of sustainability-oriented transformation processes.

Trade Unions and Just Transformations

Applicants may also investigate how trade unions contribute to shaping sustainability transformations and ensuring that these processes are socially just.

The programme is open to other research topics where the proposed project clearly contributes to its overall focus on justice, sustainability transformation and rural areas.

Academic Disciplines

The doctoral college welcomes applications from academic fields that are relevant to its research programme.

These include:

Human geography

Social sciences

Applied ethics

Economics

Sustainability science

Psychology

Research proposals from related academic fields may also be considered where they fit the overall objectives of the doctoral college.

APPLY HERE

Research Methodologies

The programme supports a range of research methodologies.

Both qualitative and quantitative research approaches are welcome.

Applicants proposing quantitative or mixed-methods research are explicitly encouraged to apply.

The comparative case study approach used by the doctoral college provides an opportunity for individual doctoral projects to contribute to a broader understanding of sustainability-oriented transformation processes.

Language Requirements

Applicants are required to have good knowledge of both German and English.

The minimum language levels specified in the call are:

German: B2

English: C1

Although German language proficiency is required for the application, the doctoral thesis may be written in English.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they can meet the required language standards before submitting their application.

Financial Support

Successful scholarship holders will receive a monthly stipend of €1,650.

The monthly funding consists of:

€1,550 basic stipend

€100 lump sum for research costs

Additional financial support may also be available.

This includes:

A health insurance contribution of up to €100

A family allowance, where applicable

The scholarships are awarded for a maximum of three years.

The standard funding period may be extended in justified cases.

Start Date and Duration

The doctoral fellowships are expected to begin between June and September 2027.

Funding can continue for a maximum of three years, subject to the applicable scholarship conditions.

The funding period is intended to provide doctoral researchers with sufficient time to develop and complete their research within the framework of the doctoral college.

Academic and Professional Development

The doctoral college offers more than financial support.

Scholarship holders will participate in an academic environment designed to encourage research development, collaboration and knowledge exchange.

The programme provides:

Thematic Workshops

Scholarship holders will have access to workshops related to the central themes of sustainability transformation and social justice.

Methodological Workshops

Researchers will also have opportunities to strengthen their methodological knowledge and research skills.

Collaborative Research Environment

The doctoral college supports collaboration among scholarship holders and participating researchers.

This is intended to create a motivating and supportive environment where researchers can exchange ideas, discuss challenges and strengthen their individual doctoral projects.

National and International Research Network

The doctoral college has established connections with national and international research institutions.

The network includes:

Leuphana University Lüneburg

Leibniz Center for Agricultural Landscape Research

Basque Center for Climate Change

Lund University

Copernicus Institute/Utrecht University

University of Vermont

These partnerships provide an opportunity to complement and deepen the expertise available within the doctoral college.

They may also provide opportunities for academic exchange and engagement with researchers working on sustainability transformation, climate change, rural development and related issues.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit the necessary application documents together with an exposé of no more than 10 pages.

The exposé should clearly outline the proposed doctoral research project and explain how it fits within the research programme of the doctoral college.

The proposal should make clear:

The research problem being addressed

The main research questions

The academic field in which the research is situated

The methodology that will be used

The sustainability transformation being examined

The justice dimensions of the research

The relevance of rural areas to the project

How the project contributes to the broader objectives of the doctoral college

Applicants should ensure that their research proposal is clearly connected to the central theme of justice dimensions of sustainability-oriented transformation processes in rural areas.

Discuss Your Research Project Before Applying

Prospective applicants are encouraged to contact the academic leadership of the doctoral college before submitting their application.

The programme indicates that promising applicants may receive support from the academic leadership in revising and adapting their exposé where necessary.

This support can help ensure that the proposed project fits the themes and requirements of the doctoral programme.

Applicants can contact:

Prof. Dr. Jana Zscheischler
Email: jana.zscheischler@uni-vechta.de

Prof. Dr. John Oliver Engler
Email: john-oliver.engler@uni-vechta.de

The exposé will subsequently undergo academic review.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Up to 3 PhD Scholarships in Germany with €1,650 Monthly Stipend at the University of Vechta

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted exclusively through the Hans Böckler Foundation’s online application portal.

Applicants should prepare the required documents and research exposé before submitting their application.

The application deadline is:

November 2, 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow enough time to prepare a well-developed research proposal.

For information about the doctoral college and its research programme, applicants can consult the University of Vechta’s VISTRA doctoral college information.

Selection Process

Doctoral fellowship decisions will be made according to BMBF guidelines and Hans Böckler Foundation selection criteria.

The application process includes academic assessment of the proposed research project.

Promising applicants may be supported in revising their exposé to better align the project with the doctoral college’s research programme and requirements.

The successful scholarship recipients are expected to be announced in May 2027.

November 2, 2026

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should pay close attention to how their proposed research connects with the central focus of the doctoral college.

A strong research proposal should clearly demonstrate:

Why the selected sustainability transformation is important

Which communities or groups are affected

What justice-related questions arise

Why rural areas are important to the research

What gap in existing research the project will address

Which research methodology will be used

Why the selected methodology is appropriate

How the project contributes to discussions on sustainability and social justice

Applicants proposing quantitative or mixed-methods projects should clearly explain how their methodological approach will help answer their research questions.

It is also advisable to contact the programme leadership before submitting the application, as the doctoral college specifically encourages prospective applicants to discuss their projects in advance.

Conclusion

The University of Vechta’s doctoral college “Justice Dimensions of Sustainability-Oriented Transformation Processes in Rural Areas” provides an opportunity for doctoral researchers to investigate some of the most important questions surrounding sustainability, social justice and rural transformation.

Up to three PhD scholarships will be awarded, with successful researchers receiving a €1,650 monthly stipend, possible additional support for health insurance and family costs, and access to thematic and methodological workshops.

The programme also offers an academic network involving national and international research institutions, providing opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Researchers working in areas such as economics, sustainability science, social sciences, human geography, applied ethics and psychology may find the programme particularly relevant, especially those developing quantitative or mixed-methods research projects.

Prospective applicants should carefully develop an exposé of no more than 10 pages and clearly demonstrate how their research fits within the doctoral college’s focus.

The application deadline is November 2, 2026. Fellowships are expected to begin between June and September 2027 and may run for up to three years.

TITLE: Contemporary Legal Issues in Higher Education Training Programme, 2024

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities in collaboration with the University of Dar-Es-Salaam presents the CONTEMPORARY LEGAL ISSUES IN HIGHER EDUCATION TRAINING PROGRAM 2024. The details of this programme are as follows: Date: 3rd December – 5th December 2024; workshop duration 3 days; Venue: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania ; Theme – Artificial Intelligence, Data Protection & 21st Century Higher Education Institutions in Africa.

TARGET AUDIENCE: This training targets all stakeholders in higher education and knowledge production with a particular focus on Innovative Institutional leaders, Policy makers, lawyers, Technology Transfer Officers, Data Protection Officers, Information Technology Professionals, Data Scientists, Academics, and Inventors.

Registration Link: https://forms.office.com/r/m4GkFy5Np6

WORKSHOP FEES: AAU member institutions: 700 USD | Non-AAU member institutions: 800 USD . This will cover workshop attendance fees, snacks and lunches, training materials, certificates, and other logistics.

BACKGROUND

In the past few decades, several actors, including regulators, students, and donors, have increasingly demanded that higher education institutions be more compliant with legal and policy frameworks in the performance of their functions. This increasing demand has exposed universities to considerable legal risk. As such, higher education institutions must be very mindful of the legal environment in which they operate. The Legal Issues in Higher Education program is an annual training program instituted by the Association of African Universities in 2017 in response to this growing need. Four training sessions have so far been held over three years in Mauritius, Botswana, and Rwanda. These training programs explored several themes relating to the legal context of higher education governance and management. The COVID pandemic in 2020 led to the truncation of this initiative.

During this lull, there have been significant legal developments in higher education. In the past five years alone, close to fifteen (15) African countries have enacted data protection legislation as well as intellectual property laws. Most of these laws raise legal issues linked to the interface of university processes to data and technology. Also, there has been significant progress in artificial intelligence in the year 2023. Generative AI in particular has provided tools that have significantly transformed innovation and inventions. This has implications for claims by Higher Education Actors to intellectual property and technology transfer. This training programme will broadly broach the key legal issues arising from this evolving environment. The purpose is to generate ideas and share perspectives on emerging legislative frameworks that address these concerns. It will also introduce participants to data management and protection policies that effectively respond to the demands imposed by legislation. The training will review related case studies based on reported litigation from the Courts.

GENERAL OVERVIEW:

The thematic areas to be focused on comprise matters relating to the interface between law, Digital Technology, Artificial Intelligence, and Intellectual Assets. The training will also explore judicial attitudes towards these issues.

METHODOLOGY/ MODE OF DELIVERY

The training session would employ the use of presentations, case studies on policy approaches, expert discussions, cohort deliberations, and open sessions, amongst others, to ensure effective facilitation, interaction, and communication of the ideals underpinning the training.

ABOUT THE FACILITATORS:

SOLOMON FAAKYE, ESQ. : Solomon Faakye is the Head of Legal and General Counsel for the University of Cape Coast (Ghana). He has also provided specialized corporate counsel to many reputable organizations including the Ghana Heritage Conservation Trust. Mr. Faakye has a deep understanding of the legal and policy environment in which higher education operates. He has broad expertise in public law and technology law. He has published widely in peer-reviewed journals both local and international and provided lectures, training, and consultancies to several reputable national and international institutions. Mr. Faakye is a recipient of several prestigious academic and professional fellowships including the Erasmus Mundus Fellowship (European Union), Quota Scholarship (Government of Norway), and Mandela Washington Fellowship (US Department of State).

PROF. NIKLAS LAVESSON: Prof. Lavesson is a full Professor of Software Engineering spec. Applied AI & Machine Learning. at Blekinge Institute of Technology, Sweden. He has held several positions in various Higher Education Institutions across Sweden. From 2017 to 2021, he was a full professor of Computer Science at the Jonkoping University, Sweden. Between 2021 to 2022, he was the senior adviser to Hamrin Foundation, Jonkoping in Sweden. Prof. Lavesson has also published in several journals including the Journal of Data Science and Analytics and the Journal of Wireless Mobile Networks, Ubiquitous Computing, and Dependable Application. His works have focused on the creation of technology, its use, and its implications on different aspects of society.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATIONS

Association of African Universities

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is an international non-governmental organization set up by the universities in Africa to promote cooperation among them and between them and the international academic community. With over 400 members across the African continent, AAU is the largest and most comprehensive organization representing Universities and Higher Education bodies in Africa. It is also the apex organization and forum for consultation, exchange of information, and cooperation among institutions of higher education in Africa, and represents the voice of higher education in Africa on regional and international bodies and supports networking by institutions of higher education in teaching, research, information exchange, and dissemination. The AAU, with headquarters in Accra, Ghana, was founded in 1967, following recommendations made at an earlier conference organized by the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) in Antananarivo, Madagascar in September 1962 for the formation of such an apex organization. The mission of the AAU is to raise the quality of higher education in Africa and strengthen its contribution to African development by fostering collaboration among its member institutions.

University of Dar es Salaam

The University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM) is Tanzania’s oldest and premier public university, established in 1961 as an affiliate of the University of London. Initially located on Lumumba Street, it moved to its current campus, known as Mlimani, in 1964. UDSM began with a single faculty, the Faculty of Law, and became a full-fledged university in 1970. It now offers more than 300 academic programs across various faculties, including PhD, Masters, undergraduate, and certificate programs. UDSM has grown significantly, with a student population of nearly 40,000 in 2020/2021, 46% of whom are female. The university emphasizes research and postgraduate training, leading to increased PhD graduations over recent years. UDSM launched Vision 2061 during its Golden Jubilee to guide future development and has introduced mid-year graduations and scholarships to support students.

TITLE: Circulation of Baffin Bay and Hudson Bay waters on the Labrador shelf and into the subpolar North Atlantic

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Duyck, E., Foukal, N., & Frajka-Williams, E. (2025). Circulation of Baffin Bay and Hudson Bay waters on the Labrador shelf and into the subpolar North Atlantic. Ocean Science, 21(1), 241–260. https://doi.org/10.5194/os-21-241-2025

Above is a new high-resolution, time-mean map of the surface velocities in the Northwest Atlantic. These velocities are derived from surface drifters drogued at 15 m depth. This new high-resolution perspective of the surface circulation in the region demonstrates the strong boundary current flow, including the coastal currents around Greenland and eastern Labrador. These currents move freshwater from Greenland and the Arctic cyclonically around the subpolar North Atlantic to the Grand Banks of Newfoundland, where much of it mixes offshore into the North Atlantic Current. Importantly, these freshwater pathways avoid the interior Labrador Sea where deep convection occurs in winter.

TITLE: MultiMiner

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
EU Projects

Image: Kati Laakso

Multi-source and Multi-scale Earth observation and Novel Machine Learning Methods for Mineral Exploration and Mine Site Monitoring

The Multi-source and Multi-scale Earth observation and Novel Machine Learning Methods for Mineral Exploration and Mine Site Monitoring (MultiMiner) project develops novel data processing algorithms for cost-effective utilization of Earth Observation (EO) technologies for mineral exploration and mine site monitoring.

MultiMiner unlocks the potential of EO data, including Copernicus, commercial satellites, upcoming missions, airborne and low altitude as well as in situ data, to support the entire mining life cycle including mineral exploration, operational, closure and post-closure stages. This is achieved by creating generic but highly innovative machine learning solutions which do not require any or only little ground truth data.

The project focuses on new EO based exploration technologies for critical raw materials (CRM) to increase the probability of finding new sources within EU thereby strengthening the EU autonomy in the area of raw materials. MultiMiner EO based exploration solutions have extremely low environmental impact, and are thus socially acceptable, economically efficient and improve safety. The project’s solutions for mine site monitoring increase the transparency of mining operations as environmental impacts can be detected as early as possible and digital information of the currently unexploitable raw materials can be stored for future generations. The applicability of the developed algorithms is demonstrated in 4 European test sites.

MultiMiner is a pan-European consortium consisting of 12 partners and 1 associated partner from research institutes, academia, consulting businesses and mining industry with interdisciplinary backgrounds in geology, remote sensing and machine learning. The members come from six EU member states which represent mining regions across Europe with diverse geology with evident potential for various types of CRM resources and thousands of operational and closed mines.

TITLE: Message of Condolence by the Association of African Universities on the passing of Professor Mohamed El-Mahrasahwy, Vice-President of the AAU and former President of Al-Azhar University

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
In Memory of Professor Mohamed El-Mahrasahwy

The Association of African Universities (AAU) expresses its profound sadness and deep sense of loss following the passing of Professor Mohamed El-Mahrasahwy, Vice-President of the AAU and former President of Al-Azhar University. Professor El-Mahrasahwy passed away in Cairo, Egypt, on Thursday, March 27, 2025.

On behalf of the AAU Governing Board and the more than 450 higher education institutions that are members of the Association, the AAU Secretariat extends its heartfelt condolences to his family, the Al-Azhar University community, and the Republic of Egypt. His visionary leadership and unwavering dedication have left an indelible mark on Africa’s academic landscape.

Professor El-Mahrasahwy was a dedicated champion of African higher education and a leader who embodied the AAU’s mission. As Vice-President since 2021, he played a pivotal role in shaping the Association’s strategic vision and programs, fostering collaboration among African universities, and advancing academic excellence. His commitment to education was further demonstrated through the establishment of the AAU’s North Africa Regional Office (NARO) and his oversight of numerous impactful initiatives and partnerships.

Born in 1962, Professor El-Mahrasahwy earned his BA in Arabic Language from the College of Arabic Language in 1985. He began his career as a teaching assistant in the Department of Linguistics at the same college, steadily rising through the ranks to become Dean in 2013. He held a master’s degree in linguistics (1992) and a PhD in linguistics (1996). His distinguished academic journey included serving as Vice President of the Islamic Universities Association since 2019, as well as holding key roles at Al-Azhar University, the Supreme Constitutional Court, and the Supreme Council of Islamic Affairs.

Professor El-Mahrasahwy’s wisdom, dedication, and guidance inspired generations of scholars, researchers, and academic leaders. His passing has created a profound void, and he will be deeply missed by the AAU community and beyond.

To honor his memory and contributions, the AAU flag will be flown at half-mast outside the Secretariat from Monday, April 1, to Monday, April 7, 2025. This gesture symbolizes the deep respect and gratitude we hold for Professor El-Mahrasahwy and his lifelong dedication to the advancement of education in Africa.

As we mourn his passing, we also celebrate his life and remarkable achievements. We reaffirm our commitment to the AAU’s mission and continue to work toward the transformation of higher education in Africa, inspired by his enduring legacy.

May his soul rest in eternal peace.

Yours in the service of higher education in Africa

Professor Olusola Oyewole

Secretary General

Association of African Universities
