TITLE: IOC Olympic Studies Centre Research Grant Programme 2027: PhD Students and Early Career Academics Invited to Apply

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) Olympic Studies Centre (OSC) has officially launched the 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme, providing an important research opportunity for emerging scholars whose academic work focuses on Olympism, the Olympic Movement, the Olympic Games, athletes, and the broader social and cultural impact of sport.

The programme is designed to support researchers at an early stage of their academic careers by providing funding that can contribute to the development and completion of scholarly research. It can also provide eligible researchers with an opportunity to access the extensive academic and historical resources held by the IOC Olympic Studies Centre in Lausanne, Switzerland.

Since the programme was established in 1999, more than 148 researchers from around the world have benefited from the initiative, receiving grants that have supported their research activities and, where appropriate, enabled them to visit the Olympic Studies Centre and consult its specialised collections.

For researchers working in the humanities and social sciences, particularly those examining the Olympic Games and their relationship with contemporary society, this programme represents a significant opportunity to advance academic research while gaining access to one of the world’s major collections of Olympic-related knowledge.

Opportunity Overview

The 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme is intended for postgraduate researchers and early-career academics undertaking research related to the Olympic world.

The programme focuses on scholarly research concerning areas such as:

Olympism and its ideals

The Olympic Movement

The Olympic Games

Olympic history

Athletes and their experiences

Sport and contemporary society

Sport and culture

The social impact of the Olympic Games

The cultural significance of Olympism

Historical, political, economic or social dimensions of the Olympic Movement

Other relevant topics within the human and social sciences that incorporate Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games as a research focus

The programme therefore goes beyond research that examines sporting competitions themselves. It can be relevant to academic projects exploring how the Olympic Movement interacts with wider questions concerning society, culture, history and contemporary life.

What Is the IOC Olympic Studies Centre?

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre is an important research and knowledge centre dedicated to Olympic studies. It provides researchers with access to specialised collections, academic publications, historical materials and other resources relating to the Olympic Movement.

Researchers interested in learning more about the centre and its activities can visit the IOC Olympic Studies Centre official website.

The centre’s resources can be particularly valuable for scholars who require historical documents, academic literature, official Olympic publications and archival material to strengthen their research.

Who Can Apply for the 2027 Research Grant Programme?

The programme is specifically targeted at current PhD students and early-career academics.

There are two principal categories of eligible applicants.

1. Current PhD Students

Current postgraduate students may apply if they are enrolled in a PhD degree programme within the human and/or social sciences and their research incorporates at least one of the following as a research focus:

Olympism

The Olympic Movement

The Olympic Games

This means that applicants do not necessarily need to be studying a programme titled “Olympic Studies.” Instead, their research should have a meaningful connection to one or more of these areas.

For example, a PhD project could potentially examine the social impact of the Olympic Games, the historical development of the Olympic Movement, the relationship between Olympism and society, the cultural significance of major sporting events, or another appropriate topic within the human and social sciences.

2. Early-Career Academics and Postdoctoral Fellows

Academic staff members and postdoctoral fellows can also be eligible.

To qualify under this category, applicants must have completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.

The eligibility provisions also recognise that the highest relevant qualification may vary depending on the academic field. In some fields, this may include a master’s degree as the equivalent highest degree.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who have recently completed their advanced academic qualifications and are beginning to establish their independent research careers.

What Can the Grant Support?

One of the most valuable aspects of the programme is its connection with the IOC Olympic Studies Centre’s research infrastructure.

Researchers who receive support can use the opportunity to advance their scholarly work and, where relevant, visit the Olympic Studies Centre in Lausanne, Switzerland to consult its collections.

This can be particularly useful for projects requiring access to primary sources, historical documentation and specialised Olympic literature.

The programme has therefore provided more than simply financial assistance to researchers. Its connection to the Olympic Studies Centre can also help scholars engage with resources that may be highly relevant to their research questions.

Access to the Olympic World Library

Researchers interested in Olympic studies can also explore the Olympic World Library (OWL), the IOC’s specialised library catalogue dedicated to Olympic knowledge.

The collection contains more than 42,000 official and academic publications, making it a valuable starting point for researchers looking for literature and documentation related to Olympic studies.

The Olympic World Library can help researchers identify relevant academic and official publications when developing their literature reviews, theoretical frameworks and research background.

The availability of such a specialised collection can be particularly valuable for PhD researchers who need to demonstrate a strong understanding of existing scholarship and historical developments within their research areas.

IOC Historical Archives

In addition to the library resources, researchers can access information about the IOC’s historical archives through the Olympic Studies Centre.

The historical archives can provide important material for scholars examining the development of the Olympic Movement, institutional history, Olympic events and other historical dimensions of Olympism.

Researchers can explore the IOC Historical Archives for further information.

For researchers undertaking historical or documentary research, these resources may provide valuable primary and contextual material that can complement conventional academic sources.

Grant Programme Selection Committee

Applications are assessed by a Grant Programme Selection Committee composed of academic experts internationally recognised for their involvement in Olympic studies, together with representatives of the Olympic Studies Centre.

The composition of the committee highlights the academic nature of the programme and the importance of the quality and relevance of applicants’ proposed research.

Applicants should therefore approach the application as a serious academic research proposal rather than simply submitting a general expression of interest.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the academic value of the research, its relationship to Olympic studies and why the proposed research requires the support and resources associated with the programme.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Although applicants should follow the official programme rules and guidelines carefully, prospective candidates should pay particular attention to the connection between their research and the programme’s objectives.

1. Clearly establish the Olympic connection

The research should have a clear and meaningful relationship with Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games.

Applicants should avoid relying on a superficial reference to sport or the Olympics. The Olympic dimension should form a genuine part of the research focus.

2. Present a clear research question

A well-defined research question can help demonstrate the academic significance of the proposed project.

Applicants should be able to explain:

What they are researching

Why the subject matters

What knowledge gap the research addresses

How the research will contribute to existing scholarship

What methods they intend to use

What sources or materials are required

3. Demonstrate academic relevance

Applicants should clearly position their proposed project within the relevant human or social sciences discipline.

This could involve explaining how the research contributes to existing discussions in fields such as history, sociology, cultural studies, political studies, economics, communication, education or another relevant discipline.

4. Make effective use of available research resources

Where appropriate, applicants should explain how the collections and resources of the Olympic Studies Centre could contribute to their research.

If a project would benefit from consulting primary sources, historical archives or specialised Olympic publications, this should be articulated clearly in the application.

5. Follow the application instructions carefully

Applicants should consult the official rules and guidelines before preparing their submission. The programme’s requirements, documentation and submission procedures should be followed precisely.

The official IOC Olympic Studies Centre page provides the central source for programme information.

Application Rules and Guidelines

The programme has published official rules and guidelines to assist prospective applicants.

Researchers should read these documents carefully before completing their application. The guidelines are particularly important because they provide the formal requirements governing the programme and the application process.

The official programme documentation should be treated as the authoritative source when determining eligibility, preparing application materials and submitting correspondence.

Application Form

Eligible researchers are required to complete the relevant application documentation provided for the programme.

Applicants should ensure that all requested information is supplied accurately and that their research proposal is presented clearly and professionally.

Before submission, candidates should check their application against the official requirements to ensure that no required component has been overlooked.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications to the 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme is Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

All application files and related correspondence should be sent to the Olympic Studies Centre before the deadline.

Deadline: 22 September 2026

Researchers should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing a competitive academic application can require considerable time, particularly where a research proposal, supporting documents or institutional information must be reviewed before submission.

Online Information Sessions

The Olympic Studies Centre is also offering two online information sessions for researchers intending to apply.

These sessions can be particularly useful for prospective applicants who want to better understand the programme and clarify aspects of the application process.

Researchers considering an application should consult the official programme rules and guidelines for information about these sessions and how they can participate.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

The main qualifying groups are

Current postgraduate students enrolled in a PhD programme within the human and/or social sciences.

PhD students whose research incorporates Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games as at least one of their research focuses.

Academic staff members who have completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.

Postdoctoral fellows who completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.

Applicants whose relevant highest qualification may be a master’s degree where the programme recognises a master’s as the equivalent highest degree for the relevant field.

Countries and Continents: Who Can Apply?

The programme is described as having benefited researchers from all over the world, and the information provided does not specify a restriction to particular countries or continents.

Therefore, the opportunity is international in scope, rather than being presented as a programme limited to a specific geographic region.

Researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other parts of the world can therefore consider applying, provided they satisfy the academic eligibility requirements.

For applicants in Africa, including researchers from Kenya and other African countries, the key consideration is not geographical location but whether the applicant meets the programme’s academic and research requirements.

However, prospective applicants should always check the official programme rules for the definitive eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

Race or Ethnicity Requirements

The information provided for the programme does not identify race or ethnicity as an eligibility restriction.

The eligibility criteria are primarily based on the applicant’s academic status, qualifications and research focus.

Consequently, applicants should focus on demonstrating that they meet the programme’s academic requirements rather than assuming that the programme is restricted to a particular racial or ethnic group.

Academic Fields Relevant to the Programme

Because the programme targets research in the human and social sciences, it may be relevant to scholars working across a variety of disciplines, provided that their research has an appropriate connection to Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games.

Potentially relevant areas may include:

History

Sociology

Political science

International relations

Cultural studies

Anthropology

Economics

Communication and media studies

Education

Sports studies

Olympic studies

Social sciences

Humanities

Other related human and social science disciplines

The decisive factor is not simply the name of the academic discipline but the relationship between the proposed research and the programme’s focus.

Another Research Grant Programme for Established Researchers

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre also offers another research opportunity for more established academics: the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme.

This programme is aimed at university professors, lecturers and research fellows who have completed their doctorate and hold an academic or research appointment.

Unlike the PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme, the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme is intended to promote advanced research by established researchers in the humanities and social sciences.

Its priority research fields are identified by the IOC every two years.

The call for applications for the 2027–2029 edition of the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme is expected to be issued in October 2026.

Researchers who are already established in academic or research positions may therefore wish to monitor the IOC Olympic Studies Centre research grant programmes page for further information.

Why This Research Grant Matters for Emerging Scholars

Research funding can be particularly important for PhD students and early-career academics because developing high-quality scholarly research often requires access to specialised literature, primary sources, archives, travel and other research resources.

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre programme offers an opportunity that combines research support with access to an internationally recognised Olympic knowledge centre.

For eligible scholars, the programme can therefore contribute to several aspects of academic development, including

Advancing an existing PhD research project

Supporting scholarly investigation into Olympic-related topics

Accessing specialised Olympic publications

Consulting historical and primary-source material

Strengthening research based on archival evidence

Developing deeper expertise in Olympic studies

Connecting academic research with the history and ideals of the Olympic Movement

Expanding the evidence base for academic publications and research outputs

The programme’s history of supporting more than 148 researchers since 1999 also demonstrates its longstanding role in supporting academic research connected to Olympic studies.

How to Apply

Researchers interested in the programme should begin by reviewing the official information provided by the Olympic Studies Centre.

A sensible application process would involve the following steps:

Step 1: Confirm your eligibility

Determine whether you are currently enrolled in a qualifying PhD programme or whether you fall within the early-career academic or postdoctoral category.

Step 2: Assess your research topic

Confirm that Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games forms at least one of the central research focuses of your project.

Step 3: Review the official rules

Read the programme rules and guidelines carefully before preparing the application.

Step 4: Prepare your application

Complete the official application form and prepare all required supporting information.

Step 5: Consider the Olympic Studies Centre resources

Determine whether the Olympic World Library, IOC historical archives or other OSC collections could contribute to your research and explain the relevance where appropriate.

Step 6: Attend an information session

Where possible, take advantage of the online information sessions offered to prospective applicants.

Step 7: Submit before the deadline

Ensure that the complete application file and related correspondence reach the Olympic Studies Centre before 22 September 2026.

APPLY HERE

For programme information and access to the relevant application resources, visit the IOC Olympic Studies Centre.

IOC Olympic Studies Centre

Conclusion

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre Research Grant Programme 2027 offers a valuable opportunity for PhD students and early-career academics seeking to advance research related to Olympism, the Olympic Movement and the Olympic Games.

Its combination of research support and access to specialised Olympic collections makes the programme particularly relevant to scholars in the humanities and social sciences who require high-quality academic, historical and primary-source material for their work.

The programme is international in scope and is aimed at researchers who meet the specified academic and research criteria, rather than being restricted to applicants from a particular country, continent, race or ethnicity.

With more than 148 researchers having benefited from the programme since its establishment in 1999, the initiative has a longstanding history of supporting scholarship in Olympic studies.

Eligible researchers should carefully review the official rules, prepare a strong and clearly focused research proposal, take advantage of the available information sessions and ensure that their complete application is submitted before the 22 September 2026 deadline.

TITLE: UNU–University of Bonn Joint MSc 2027: Applications Open with Fully Funded DAAD EPOS Scholarships

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are open for the 2027 intake of the Joint Master of Science in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security, an international postgraduate programme jointly offered by the United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security and the Department of Geography at the University of Bonn.

The two-year, full-time programme is delivered in Bonn, Germany, and combines advanced academic study with practical training in environmental risks, climate change, disaster management, human security, vulnerability, resilience and sustainable development.

A limited number of fully funded scholarships are available through the German Academic Exchange Service’s Development-Related Postgraduate Courses programme, commonly known as DAAD EPOS. These scholarships are intended for qualified professionals from eligible developing and emerging countries who have relevant postgraduate work experience and plan to continue working as development practitioners after completing the degree.

Applications for the October 2027 intake must be completed by 31 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time. Both the online application and the complete application documents submitted by email must be received before the deadline.

Programme Summary

Programme: Joint Master of Science in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security

Institutions: United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security and University of Bonn

Degree level: Master of Science

Programme location: Bonn, Germany

Study format: Full-time and residential

Programme duration: Two years

Normal study period: Four semesters

Programme start: October 2027

Application opening date: 31 July 2026

Application deadline: 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET

Teaching language: English

Minimum English level: B2

Recommended English level: C1

Tuition fees: None

University semester contribution: Approximately €310 per semester

Additional UNU contribution: €100 for each of the first three semesters

Scholarship opportunity: Limited fully funded DAAD EPOS scholarships

Compulsory internship: At least eight weeks

Application method: Online form followed by submission of application documents by email

Application email: master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu

Official programme page: Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security

Online application: Start the 2027 programme application

About the Joint Master’s Programme

The Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security was developed to provide postgraduate students with the theoretical knowledge, research methods and practical tools necessary to understand environmental risks and their consequences for societies.

The programme examines how natural hazards and environmental changes emerge, how they affect human-nature relationships and why certain communities, regions and population groups are more vulnerable than others.

Students investigate concepts such as:

Environmental risk

Natural hazards

Human security

Social and environmental vulnerability

Community and institutional resilience

Climate change adaptation

Disaster risk reduction

Risk governance

Sustainable development

Human-nature relationships

Humanitarian response

Earth system science

Environmental policy

The programme combines the academic strengths of the University of Bonn’s Department of Geography with the applied, policy-oriented and international research environment of UNU-EHS.

This collaboration enables students to study environmental risks from both physical and human geography perspectives while connecting their academic learning to international development, policymaking and humanitarian practice.

The official 2027 call for applications highlights the programme’s strong interest in environmental risk governance, human-nature relations and challenges facing the Global South.

Main Objectives of the Programme

The programme aims to:

Develop advanced theoretical and methodological expertise in environmental risks and human security

Connect academic knowledge with practical experience

Examine vulnerability, resilience and adaptation in different geographical contexts

Maintain a strong focus on developing countries and the Global South

Create an intercultural and interdisciplinary learning environment

Strengthen students’ qualitative and quantitative research capabilities

Develop competence in geographical information systems and remote sensing

Provide opportunities to participate in research projects at UNU-EHS and the University of Bonn

Facilitate interaction with the United Nations system and other international organisations

Prepare graduates for professional careers in development, climate adaptation, disaster risk reduction, humanitarian work, environmental governance and related fields

Academic Areas Covered by the Programme

The programme brings together a wide range of fields and research interests, including:

Vulnerability assessment

Ecosystem services

Sustainable development

Disaster management

Disaster risk reduction

Climate change adaptation

Human-nature relationships

Science and technology studies

Development geography

Geomorphology

Socio-hydrology

Future studies

Geographic information systems

Remote sensing

Risk management

Human security

Risk forecasting and prediction

Humanitarian response

Environmental policy and governance

This combination allows students to evaluate environmental risks as interconnected physical, social, political, technological and economic challenges.

Programme Curriculum and Modules

The Joint MSc consists of 12 modules. Ten modules are principally taught during the first three semesters. The programme then includes a compulsory internship, a master’s colloquium and independent work on the master’s thesis.

Major modules include:

Theories and Concepts of Risk

This module introduces the central theories and conceptual approaches used to understand environmental risks, hazards, vulnerability, resilience and human security.

General Approaches to Risk and Human Security

Students examine new approaches to development geography and Earth system science, connecting social and physical processes.

Research Methods

This module develops the methodological skills required to design, conduct and evaluate interdisciplinary research.

Academic Writing and Intercultural Skills

Students strengthen academic communication, structured scientific writing and intercultural collaboration.

Advanced Debates on Risk and Human Security

The module examines contemporary academic and policy debates surrounding environmental change, social vulnerability and human security.

Research Seminar

Students participate in applied research and project-based work connected to environmental risks and human security.

Academic Presentation and Communication Skills

This module develops the ability to present complex scientific findings clearly to academic, professional and policy audiences.

Risk Management in the Context of Climate Change

Students study climate-related risks, adaptation strategies, governance arrangements and practical risk-management approaches.

Disaster Management and Humanitarian Response

The programme examines disaster preparedness, emergency response, humanitarian systems and disaster risk reduction.

Field Trips

Students participate in field-based learning activities lasting at least three days and prepare an associated report.

Compulsory Internship

Students must complete an internship of at least eight weeks. The internship must be directly connected to the subject matter of the programme.

Students receive support in searching for suitable opportunities, but the programme does not automatically place students with an internship host.

Master’s Colloquium and Thesis

Students develop and present their research proposal through the master’s colloquium before completing an independent master’s thesis.

The thesis carries 30 credit points and is normally completed over six months. Students must have earned at least 60 credit points before beginning the thesis.

The current programme structure can be reviewed in the official curriculum overview.

General Academic Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a first higher education qualification, normally a bachelor’s degree or an equivalent recognised qualification, in Geography or a closely related and relevant academic discipline.

The selection committee reviews all academic achievements, including:

Bachelor’s-level coursework

Any completed master’s-level coursework

Exchange-semester credits

Summer schools

Additional university courses

Other recognised academic studies

The majority of the applicant’s completed coursework must relate to the following three areas:

1. Human Geography and Social Sciences

Relevant subjects should focus on topics such as:

Spatial patterns

Society

Development

Human geography

Population and settlement

Social vulnerability

Regional development

Human-environment relationships

2. Scientific Methodology and Empirical Research

Applicants should have studied research-related subjects, including:

Scientific research design

Qualitative methods

Quantitative methods

Data collection

Statistical or empirical analysis

Field research

Academic writing

Research methodology

3. Physical Geography, Geosciences and Environmental Sciences

Relevant coursework should address areas such as:

Earth system science

Physical geography

Environmental systems

Geosciences

Climate processes

Natural hazards

Ecosystems

Environmental change

Applicants should carefully compare their academic transcripts with these three areas before applying. The final decision regarding the relevance and adequacy of previous academic study can only be made by the programme’s selection committee after reviewing the complete application.

Applicants Who May Not Be Eligible

The programme is not principally designed for applicants whose academic background is dominated by engineering subjects.

Graduates of International Relations or similar programmes will generally not be considered unless their academic profile has a strong and demonstrable connection with environmental risks.

Current PhD students and people who already hold a PhD are not eligible for this master’s programme.

Applicants with multidisciplinary degrees should not rely only on the title of their qualification. Their transcripts must show that most of their academic coursework is relevant to human geography, research methods and environmental or Earth system sciences.

Can Final-Year Bachelor’s Students Apply?

Applicants who will complete their bachelor’s degree after the application deadline may submit an application using their current transcripts.

If admitted, they must subsequently provide their final transcript and bachelor’s degree certificate. The qualifying degree must be completed before the Joint MSc begins in October 2027.

Motivation Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate a strong and genuine motivation to contribute to the fields of human security, environmental change and risk management.

The programme seeks applicants who are:

Interested in interdisciplinary research

Prepared to study in a multicultural academic environment

Motivated to address environmental and development challenges

Capable of connecting scientific knowledge with practical solutions

Interested in environmental risks affecting developing countries and the Global South

Able to explain how the programme relates to their future career

The required programme motivation letter must specifically address:

The applicant’s academic background

Relevant professional experience

Knowledge of the programme curriculum

Particular scientific interests

Future career aspirations

How the programme will support those aspirations

The applicant’s suitability for the programme

Applicants currently enrolled in another postgraduate programme must explain why they intend to leave or change their existing programme.

English-Language Requirements

The programme is taught in English. Applicants must demonstrate at least B2 proficiency under the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, although C1 proficiency is recommended.

Merely completing a degree taught in English does not automatically exempt an applicant from submitting a recognised language certificate.

The following tests and minimum results are accepted:

English test
Minimum score

TOEFL Paper-Based Test
550

TOEFL Internet-Based Test
79

TOEFL Computer-Based Test
213

IELTS Academic
6.5

Cambridge Advanced English
At least B2

Cambridge Proficiency in English
Accepted

telc English
B2–C1

Pearson Test of English Academic

Duolingo English Test
120

Native English speakers from the following countries are exempt from providing a language certificate:

Australia

Canada

Republic of Ireland

New Zealand

United Kingdom

United States

German applicants who completed the relevant advanced English course through the “Leistungskurs Abitur” may provide suitable documentation in place of one of the listed tests.

Applicants should consult the official programme requirements and FAQs before selecting or booking an English test.

DAAD EPOS Fully Funded Scholarship

The Joint MSc is among the selected development-related postgraduate programmes supported through the DAAD EPOS funding scheme.

A limited number of fully funded scholarships may be awarded to highly qualified applicants from eligible developing and emerging countries.

Admission to the master’s programme does not guarantee a DAAD EPOS scholarship. Applicants can be admitted academically without receiving funding and may then choose to enrol as self-funded students.

DAAD EPOS Scholarship Benefits

According to the current DAAD EPOS scholarship information, funding for graduate-level scholarship holders may include:

A monthly scholarship payment of €992

Payments toward health insurance

Payments toward accident insurance

Personal liability insurance coverage

A travel allowance, unless travel costs are covered by another source

Depending on individual circumstances, recipients may also receive:

A monthly rent subsidy

An allowance for accompanying family members

Applicants should consult the current DAAD call and their eventual scholarship award documents for the final financial conditions.

Additional DAAD EPOS Eligibility Requirements

Candidates seeking the DAAD EPOS scholarship must satisfy the general academic requirements of the master’s programme and the following additional conditions:

Be from an eligible developing or emerging country

Hold an appropriate bachelor’s degree

Have strong academic results, normally placing them within the upper third of their graduating group

Have accumulated at least two years of relevant professional experience after completing the bachelor’s degree

Complete the required two years of experience by the application deadline

Have obtained their most recent academic degree no more than six years before the application deadline

Not already hold another master’s degree in a similar field

Intend to pursue a practitioner-oriented career in development after graduation

Not use the scholarship principally as preparation for an academic career or PhD

Demonstrate development-related motivation

Be prepared to take social responsibility and support positive change in their professional environment

Commit fully to completing the Joint MSc if selected

Normally not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months by the application deadline

Relevant professional experience may have been acquired through:

A government organisation

A public authority

A non-governmental organisation

A state-owned organisation

A private company

A development agency

Another professional institution working in a relevant field

Only work experience obtained after completion of the bachelor’s degree is counted toward the two-year requirement. Experience accumulated after the application deadline cannot be included.

Tuition Fees and Other Study Charges

There are no tuition fees for the Joint MSc.

Students are nevertheless required to pay certain institutional contributions:

Approximately €310 per semester to the University of Bonn, including the local public-transportation ticket

€100 to UNU for each of the first three semesters

These amounts do not include accommodation, food, personal expenses, visa costs or other living expenses in Bonn. Institutional contributions may also change before enrolment.

The programme is full-time and residential. It cannot be completed remotely or on a part-time basis, and students must live in or near Bonn so they can attend classes.

Documents Required from All Applicants

Applicants must arrange their documents in the exact order prescribed by the programme.

1. Online Application Confirmation

After completing the online application form, applicants will receive confirmation by email. This confirmation must be signed, dated and included as a scanned document in the application package.

2. Programme Motivation Letter

The motivation letter must:

Be between one and two pages

Be dated

Explain the applicant’s academic and professional suitability

Demonstrate knowledge of the programme

Identify specific scientific interests

Explain future career aspirations

Describe how the programme will benefit the applicant

3. Europass Curriculum Vitae

The CV must:

Use the Europass format

Be arranged in reverse chronological order

Not exceed three pages

Be signed and dated

Include exact dates

Correspond precisely with the dates appearing in supporting references and certificates

4. Academic Degree Certificates

Applicants should submit:

Bachelor’s degree certificate or equivalent

Master’s degree certificate, if available

Certified translations where documents are not in English or German

DAAD EPOS applicants must ensure that the original academic certificate has been signed or stamped by the issuing university.

5. Academic Transcripts

Transcripts should cover the bachelor’s degree, any available master’s study and other relevant academic credits.

The transcripts must:

Be in English or German or accompanied by certified translations

Show an identifiable overall average grade

Include an explanation of the applicable grading system, except for German qualifications

Include relevant exchange semesters, summer schools and additional credits

For DAAD EPOS applicants, transcripts must be stamped by the issuing university or sent directly by the university registrar to master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu.

6. Proof of English Proficiency

Applicants must provide one of the accepted English-language certificates unless they qualify for a specified exemption.

7. Academic References

Academic references are recommended but optional.

Applicants may provide no more than two references from former university lecturers. Each reference should:

Be recent

Be dated

Be signed and stamped

Appear on official letterhead

Be written in English or German or accompanied by a certified translation

8. Passport Copy

Submit the passport page displaying the applicant’s name and personal information.

9. Other Relevant References

Applicants may submit up to three additional references covering relevant:

Employment

Internships

Professional training

Volunteering

Practical experience

School certificates should not be included.

10. APS Certificate Where Applicable

Applicants from China, India and Viet Nam must include a scan of their applicable Academic Evaluation Centre certificate.

Additional Documents for DAAD EPOS Applicants

Scholarship applicants must also include:

1. DAAD EPOS Checklist

The required checklist must be completed, dated and signed on the specified page. DAAD requires a handwritten signature; a digitally inserted signature is not accepted.

2. DAAD Application Form

The form must:

Be completed electronically rather than by hand

Be dated

Identify every EPOS programme for which the applicant is applying

List programme preferences in the required order

Applicants may normally apply for a maximum of three EPOS courses and must explain their priorities consistently.

3. Scholarship Motivation Letter

The scholarship motivation letter must be between one and two pages and must be dated.

It may build upon the general programme motivation letter, but it must additionally explain:

Why the applicant is seeking a DAAD scholarship

Why the applicant wants to study in Germany

How the application is related to development

How the scholarship will support the applicant’s professional ambitions

How the applicant expects to contribute as a development practitioner

The applicant’s programme preferences if applying to more than one EPOS course

4. Professional Reference from the Current Employer

The reference must:

Be recent

Be dated

Be signed and stamped

Be issued on official letterhead

Come from the employer, supervisor or human resources department

Be written in English or German or accompanied by a certified translation

5. Employment Certificates

The certificates must:

Document at least two years of relevant work experience after the bachelor’s degree

State the precise starting and ending dates in day-month-year format

Be issued by an authorised person

Be dated

Be signed and stamped

Appear on official letterhead

Mandatory Academic Writing Sample

Every applicant must submit a separate academic writing sample in English for the 2027 intake.

The essay should explain:

How the applicant’s academic or professional experiences have influenced the subjects they want to explore during the master’s programme

How those experiences could contribute to a possible master’s thesis

Why the proposed perspective could help address an identifiable research gap

The writing sample must:

Be written as an academic essay

Be no longer than 1,000 words, excluding references

Draw upon relevant scientific literature

Use no more than 10 references

Follow APA referencing style

Be original work written personally by the applicant

Be submitted as a separate PDF

Include the required declaration of authenticity

The programme requires applicants to add the following declaration:

“I confirm to have written the essay myself, without the use of AI.”

The programme warns that plagiarism and artificial-intelligence checks may be applied. Applicants must therefore write the academic essay independently and should not submit AI-generated or plagiarised work.

Required Application Format

Applicants must comply with the following submission rules:

Complete the online application form first

Download or obtain the application confirmation sent by email

Sign and date the required confirmation

Submit the documents in the exact prescribed order

Merge the main documents into one PDF

Ensure the merged PDF does not exceed 8MB

Name the application file as: LastName.FirstName.pdf

Submit the academic writing sample as a separate PDF

Use a separate email for the writing sample if attachment limits make this necessary

Submit scans rather than smartphone photographs

Use certified translations where required

Do not send original documents

Do not send a paper application through the post

Ensure the complete package is received before the deadline

Applicants may be asked to present original certificates for verification after admission.

Step-by-Step Application Process

Step 1: Review the Eligibility Criteria

Check the programme requirements, academic subject requirements, English-language conditions and DAAD EPOS criteria where applicable.

Step 2: Complete the Online Application Form

Submit the official 2027 online application form.

The form can only be submitted once. Applicants who are not ready to complete it in one session should use the “Save and Continue Later” option.

Step 3: Receive and Sign the Confirmation

After submitting the online form, obtain the confirmation sent by email. Sign and date it as instructed.

Step 4: Prepare the Main Application Package

Arrange all required documents in the exact prescribed order and merge them into one PDF not exceeding 8MB.

Step 5: Prepare the Academic Writing Sample

Save the original academic essay as a separate PDF and include the required declaration of authenticity.

Step 6: Email the Application

Send the complete package to:

master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu

Both the online form and emailed application documents must be received by the deadline.

Applications sent directly to DAAD at the initial stage will not be forwarded to the programme.

Selection Process

The number of places is limited, and admission is regulated through a local Numerus Clausus selection process.

The selection committee considers:

Academic performance

Relevance of previous academic coursework

Research and methodological preparation

Ability to communicate at a scientific level

Quality of the academic writing sample

Motivation

Career plans

Relevant professional experience

Overall suitability for the programme

Formally complete applications are first assessed for academic eligibility.

Suitable candidates are expected to be shortlisted and invited to an interview in January or February 2027. The interview may assess their academic and professional background, motivation, career objectives and overall fit.

Candidates shortlisted for DAAD EPOS funding are subsequently forwarded to DAAD. The EPOS selection process is expected to take place between February and April.

Applicants are expected to receive a final update on their application status around April or May 2027.

An applicant who is admitted to the programme but is not awarded the DAAD EPOS scholarship may still accept the place as a self-funded student.

Can Admission Be Deferred?

Admission cannot be deferred to the following year.

An admitted applicant who cannot begin the programme in October 2027 will lose the place, which may be offered to another candidate on the waiting list. The applicant would need to submit a new application for a future intake.

Career Opportunities

Graduates can pursue careers in organisations working on environmental change, risk management, human security and international development.

Potential employers and sectors include:

United Nations agencies

International organisations

Government ministries and public authorities

Federal agencies

Development organisations

Humanitarian agencies

Non-governmental organisations

Research institutes

Universities and academic institutions

Environmental consultancies

Private companies

Disaster preparedness organisations

Climate change and sustainability programmes

Food-security organisations

Spatial-planning institutions

Environmental and development-policy bodies

Potential areas of work include:

Disaster risk reduction

Disaster preparedness

Humanitarian response

Climate change adaptation

Environmental risk assessment

Human security

Sustainable development

Vulnerability and resilience analysis

Environmental policy

Geographic information systems

Remote sensing

Food security

Spatial planning

Risk governance

International development

Research and policy analysis

Important Application Deadline

The application deadline for the October 2027 intake is:

31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET, Bonn, Germany time.

The application period runs from 31 July to 31 October 2026.

Late, incomplete and paper applications will not be considered. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the process requires both an online submission and a complete email application package.

Application Links and Contact Information

Official programme information: UNU-EHS Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security

Online application form: Apply for the October 2027 intake

DAAD EPOS scholarship information: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses

Programme email: master-georisk@ehs.unu.edu

Conclusion

The Joint MSc in Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security provides an exceptional opportunity to study environmental risks, climate adaptation, disaster management and human security within the combined academic environments of the United Nations University and the University of Bonn.

Its interdisciplinary curriculum, research opportunities, compulsory internship and connection with the United Nations system make it particularly relevant for professionals seeking careers in environmental governance, disaster risk reduction, humanitarian response, international development and climate policy.

Applicants from eligible developing and emerging countries may also compete for a limited number of fully funded DAAD EPOS scholarships. Scholarship candidates must demonstrate strong academic performance, at least two years of relevant postgraduate professional experience, development-related motivation and a clear intention to continue working as practitioners after graduation.

Prospective candidates should examine their academic transcripts carefully, arrange their English-language evidence, prepare all certificates in the required format and write the mandatory academic essay independently. The complete online and email applications must reach the programme no later than 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Adam J. Grotsky

Executive Director, USIEF

Adam Grotsky is the Executive Director of the United States-India Educational Foundation (USIEF), the Fulbright Commission in India, a position he has held since May 2008. He oversees the Fulbright-Nehru Program and EducationUSA India, working to strengthen educational partnerships and people-to-people ties between the United States and India through academic exchange.

During his tenure, USIEF has administered more than 4,000 Fulbright-Nehru fellowships to students, scholars, researchers, teachers, and professionals from both countries. Under his leadership, the Foundation has expanded opportunities for academic collaboration, fostered institutional partnerships, and supported thousands of emerging and established leaders whose work has strengthened one of the world’s most important bilateral relationships.

Before joining USIEF, Mr. Grotsky served as Director of Study Abroad at Towson University in Maryland and, prior to that, as Associate Director for International Programs at the University of South Carolina. He began his career in international education as Resident Director of the University of Wisconsin’s College Year in India Program in Varanasi, an experience that launched a lifelong commitment to educational exchange and U.S.-India relations.

With more than thirty years of experience in international education, Mr. Grotsky has been a strong advocate for the transformative power of educational exchange to promote mutual understanding, develop future leaders, and build lasting international partnerships.

Mr. Grotsky earned a B.A. in Political Science from the University of Pennsylvania and an M.A. in South Asian Studies from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

TITLE: 2027-2028 Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral Research Fellowships

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications submitted prior to February 18, 2026 will NOT BE considered.

The Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral Research Fellowships are designed to build long-term capacity to address global challenges and develop innovative solutions in key priority areas in both India and the U.S. We encourage proposals that are futuristic, innovative and technology focused.

Selected scholars will have the opportunity to conduct research, audit non-degree courses at U.S. academic institutions to enhance their knowledge and gain practical work experience in suitable settings in the U.S.

These fellowships are designed for Indian scholars who are registered for a Ph.D. at an Indian institution. These fellowships are for six to nine months.

Fields of Study

1. Critical Minerals and Supply Chains

Geology

Materials Science

Mining Engineering

4. Science and Research Collaboration

Bioengineering

Artificial Intelligence

Semiconductor Engineering

2. Defense and Security

Cybersecurity

Aerospace Engineering

Robotics and Autonomous Systems

5. Space Cooperation

Astrophysics

Planetary Science

Space Systems Engineering

Satellite Communications

3. Energy Security

Energy Engineering

Petroleum Engineering

Energy Innovation and Technology Commercialization

6. Technology and Innovation

Data Science

Quantum Computing

Electrical and Electronics Engineering

Affiliation

The applicant will be affiliated to one U.S. host institution. USIEF strongly recommends all applicants to indicate affiliation preference, and to correspond, in advance, with potential host institutions. If the applicant has secured a letter of invitation from a U.S. institution, they must include it as a part of the online application.

Grant Benefits

The fellowships provide J-1 visa support, a monthly stipend, Accident and Sickness Program for Exchanges per U.S. Government guidelines, round-trip economy class air travel, applicable allowances and modest affiliation fees, if any. No allowances are provided for dependents. The grant is not sufficient to support family members.

Eligibility Requirements

In addition to the General Prerequisites

This grant is intended for Ph.D. students to conduct research essential to their dissertations/thesis. Therefore, the expected Ph.D. thesis submission date should be at least three months after the Fulbright-Nehru grant end date. For example, if May 2028 is the grant end date, the applicant cannot submit their thesis before August 2028. Please indicate the Ph.D. registration date and the expected Ph.D. thesis submission date in the Applicant Annexure.

The applicant should provide clear justification on the need for undertaking research in the U.S. and the U.S. institution identified for the research. They should have done reasonable study pertaining to their research objectives, especially in the identification of resources in India and the U.S.

Applicant must be registered for Ph.D. at an Indian institution on or before November 1, 2025. On the online application form, one of the recommendation letters must be from the Ph.D. supervisor that comments on applicants’ research, need for the fellowship, and must indicate the Ph.D. registration date and topic.

If the applicant is employed, they must follow the instructions carefully regarding employer’s endorsement. If applicable, please obtain the endorsement from the appropriate administrative authority on the FNDR Employer’s Endorsement Form. The employer must indicate that leave will be granted for the fellowship period; and

The applicant must upload a copy of the original published/presented paper or extracts from the Masters’/M.Phil. thesis on the online application form (not exceeding 20 pages).

Employees of the Government of India and Indian State Governments are not eligible for any Fulbright-Nehru Fellowships. This includes civil servants in central services (such as IAS, IPS, IRS, IFS, and allied services), state government services (including state civil services), and bureaucratic staff employed in central and state ministries or departments. However, researchers, scientists, and academicians from CSIR, ICAR, ICGEB, DRDO, ISRO, ICMR, DBT institutions, DST laboratories, BARC, IISc, and IITs, as well as other centrally funded government institutions and universities, are eligible to apply.

TITLE: RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call for Applications | Regional Conference of Youth in Accra, Ghana

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) Africa 2026 is inviting young Africans to apply for delegate participation in the upcoming regional youth climate conference, taking place in Accra, Ghana, from 18–21 October 2026.

RCOY Africa brings together young climate leaders, researchers, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, civil society representatives, Indigenous Peoples, and development partners to strengthen youth participation in Africa’s climate agenda.

The 2026 conference will provide a platform for young people across Africa to exchange ideas, develop regional solutions, strengthen their technical knowledge, and contribute to youth priorities ahead of COP31.

About RCOY Africa 2026

The Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) is the regional edition of the Conference of Youth (COY), held ahead of the annual United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conference of the Parties.

RCOY Africa serves as a major platform for African youth engagement in the global climate process.

The conference builds on the outcomes and recommendations generated through Local Conferences of Youth (LCOYs) organised across African countries. These national youth perspectives are brought together at the regional level to help develop a unified African youth position.

The outcomes of RCOY Africa 2026 are intended to contribute to the global youth agenda and inform youth engagement at COP31.

RCOY Africa 2026 Theme

The theme of the 2026 conference is:

“Driving Integrated Solutions Across Africa’s Climate Agenda for Impact, Resilience and Justice.”

The theme reflects the need for coordinated and inclusive approaches to addressing Africa’s climate challenges while promoting resilience, justice, and meaningful impact.

Who Should Apply?

The RCOY Africa 2026 delegate application is open to young people who meet the basic eligibility requirements and can demonstrate meaningful engagement with climate-related issues.

Applicants must:

Be between 18 and 35 years old at the time of the conference.

Be a citizen or resident of an African country.

Demonstrate an interest or engagement in climate-related issues.

Be able to contribute meaningfully to conference discussions and activities.

The selection process is competitive because the number of fully and partially funded places is limited.

Selection Criteria

Applications will be assessed based on several factors, including:

Motivation

Applicants should demonstrate a clear motivation for participating in RCOY Africa 2026 and explain why the conference is relevant to their work, interests, experience, or aspirations.

Leadership

Demonstrated leadership experience will be considered as part of the selection process.

This may include leadership in climate initiatives, youth organisations, community projects, research, advocacy, entrepreneurship, or other relevant activities.

Climate Engagement

Applicants should demonstrate meaningful involvement or interest in climate action and related areas.

This could include work or engagement in areas such as climate policy, climate justice, environmental sustainability, adaptation, mitigation, renewable energy, biodiversity, youth advocacy, or community resilience.

Diversity and Inclusion

The selection process will also consider diversity and inclusion to ensure broad representation among participating delegates.

Regional Representation

Applicants from different African countries and regions will be considered to support broad regional representation at the conference.

Potential Contribution

Applicants will also be assessed based on their potential to contribute meaningfully to discussions, activities, knowledge exchange, and the wider objectives of RCOY Africa 2026.

Funding and Participation

Participation is competitive, and fully and partially funded delegate opportunities are limited.

The information provided for the call does not specify that every selected participant will receive full funding. Applicants should therefore carefully review the application information and any communication from the organisers regarding the specific funding arrangement attached to their selection.

Conference Location and Dates

Event: Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) Africa 2026

Location: Accra, Ghana

Dates: 18–21 October 2026

Age Range: 18–35 years

Eligible Region: African countries

Important Application Requirement

Applicants are specifically required to complete the application in their own words.

The organisers state that the use of generative AI to write application responses is not permitted.

Applicants should therefore ensure that all personal statements, motivation responses, and other written answers submitted through the application form accurately reflect their own experiences, perspectives, and ideas.

Using AI-generated responses could conflict with the organisers’ application requirements.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call is:

Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 11:59 PM GMT

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official online application form and provide the information requested by the organisers.

Application Form: Apply for RCOY Africa 2026

Applicants should carefully read each question and provide accurate information based on their own experiences.

For questions or enquiries about the application, applicants can contact:

Email: rcoyafrica2026@gmail.com

Why RCOY Africa 2026 Matters

RCOY Africa provides an important platform for young Africans to participate in conversations surrounding the continent’s climate future.

Africa faces significant climate-related challenges, including vulnerability to extreme weather events, food and water insecurity, climate-induced displacement, ecosystem degradation, and challenges associated with sustainable development.

Young people have an important role to play in developing and advocating for solutions to these challenges.

Through RCOY Africa, participants can engage with other young leaders and stakeholders, exchange knowledge, strengthen regional collaboration, and contribute African youth perspectives to the broader international climate process.

Connection to COP31

One of the important functions of RCOY Africa is to help consolidate youth perspectives ahead of the annual UN climate negotiations.

The 2026 regional conference will build on recommendations from Local Conferences of Youth across Africa and help bring together national perspectives into a broader African youth position.

This provides participants with an opportunity to contribute to discussions that can inform youth engagement in the international climate process leading towards COP31.

What Kind of Applicants Should Consider Applying?

The call may be particularly relevant to young Africans involved in or interested in:

Climate change

Climate policy

Climate justice

Environmental sustainability

Renewable energy

Climate adaptation

Climate mitigation

Sustainable development

Environmental advocacy

Youth leadership

Research and innovation

Green entrepreneurship

Community development

Resilience building

International climate negotiations

Applicants do not necessarily need to come from one specific academic discipline. What is particularly important is their demonstrated interest, engagement, leadership, motivation, and potential contribution to the conference.

Application Tips

Before submitting your application, consider the following:

Check your eligibility: Confirm that you are 18–35 years old and a citizen or resident of an African country.

Use your own words: The organisers explicitly prohibit the use of generative AI to write application responses.

Be authentic: Your responses should accurately describe your experiences, climate engagement, leadership journey, and motivation.

Demonstrate impact: Where appropriate, explain what you have done rather than simply stating that you are interested in climate action.

Explain your motivation: Clearly communicate why participating in RCOY Africa 2026 matters to you.

Submit early: Do not wait until the final hours before the deadline to complete the application.

Review before submitting: Check that all required sections have been completed and that your information is accurate.

Conclusion

The RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call for Applications offers young Africans an opportunity to participate in a major regional youth climate platform in Accra, Ghana, from 18–21 October 2026.

With a focus on impact, resilience, justice, regional collaboration, and integrated climate solutions, the conference will bring together young people and other stakeholders working to advance Africa’s climate priorities.

Eligible young Africans between 18 and 35 years old who are citizens or residents of African countries are encouraged to consider applying. Because funded spaces are limited and the selection process is competitive, applicants should prepare their applications carefully and submit them before the 9 September 2026 deadline.

Most importantly, applicants should remember that the organisers require application responses to be written in the applicant’s own words and do not permit generative AI to write those responses.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

TITLE: Nederlands Letterenfonds Fellowship Programme 2026 (€3,500 stipend)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: August 25, 2026

Applications are open for the Nederlands Letterenfonds Fellowship Programme 2026. The Letterenfonds Fellowship is a continuation of the Writer-in-Residence programme and part of the longstanding collaboration between NIAS and the Dutch Foundation for Literature (Nederlands Letterenfonds). The programme fosters transdisciplinary exchange between writers, and scholars from the humanities, social sciences and other disciplines. The fellowship allows writers to devote themselves full-time to a writing project of their choice within a diverse community of international scholars.

For this edition, NIAS and the Dutch Foundation for Literature specifically invite applications from writers based in the Caribbean Parts of the Kingdom. The fellowship aims to strengthen the presence of literary voices from the Caribbean within the NIAS community and to encourage exchange between literature, scholarship and society across the Kingdom.

Benefits

The fellow receives a personal stipend of €3,500 per month.

The fellow is provided travel reimbursement of an international return ticket.

The fellow is provided with an office at NIAS, access to research facilities, and subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam.

The fellow benefits from and participates in weekly academic seminars and interdisciplinary dialogue.

A residency at the Institute constitutes a full-time commitment and fellows are expected to be present at the Institute four workdays a week from the opening of their semester until the end of their semester.

Eligibility

The fellowship is open to literary fiction and non-fiction writers based in the Caribbean Parts of the Kingdom (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten) who write in Papiamentu, Papiamento, English from the Islands or Dutch. Applicants should be established writers with a literary track record and a body of work that demonstrates sustained literary quality and professional practice.

The fellowship is intended for writers at a mid-career or senior stage who are comfortable working within an academic and international environment and who are eager to engage in intellectual exchange with scholars from different disciplines.

Applicants must propose a literary project that will clearly benefit from a residency at NIAS. The project should already be beyond its initial conception phase and be sufficiently developed to make productive use of the fellowship period.

Eligible candidates are expected to participate actively in the NIAS community through seminars, workshops and informal exchanges with other fellows. As English is the working language at NIAS, applicants must have a good command of English.
