TITLE: University of Sussex Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027 in UK

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The University of Sussex Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027 are an excellent opportunity for students from eligible low-income Commonwealth countries who want to pursue a PhD in UK. These fully funded PhD scholarships in UK support talented and motivated candidates who cannot afford to study in UK without financial assistance. The international scholarships for PhD aim to help students gain advanced knowledge and skills that can contribute to sustainable development in their home countries.

The University of Sussex Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027 are funded by the UK Department for International Development (DFID) and support full-time doctoral study. The fully funded scholarship in UK covers full overseas PhD tuition fees, provides a stipend, and supports return travel to the UK. Students can also receive a Research Training Support Grant and funding for eligible fieldwork costs. Therefore, these University of Sussex PhD scholarships offer comprehensive financial support for international students pursuing doctoral studies in the UK.

The Commonwealth PhD Scholarships are available under six development-focused themes. These include science and technology for development, strengthening health systems and capacity, promoting global prosperity, strengthening global peace, security and governance, strengthening resilience and response to crises, and access, inclusion and opportunity. Students can choose research that aligns with one of these themes and demonstrates a clear development impact.

Applicants from countries including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Sri Lanka, Rwanda, Uganda, Zambia, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, and other eligible Commonwealth countries can apply. However, applicants must meet specific academic, financial, nationality, and residency requirements. They must also secure support from a University of Sussex supervisor and complete the required applications before the scholarship deadline.

These fully funded scholarships in UK provide an excellent opportunity for students who want to pursue a PhD while contributing to development in their home countries. If you want to study at the University of Sussex with full financial support, check the eligibility criteria and application requirements for the University of Sussex Commonwealth Scholarships 2027 and apply before the deadline.

TITLE: Workshop on Safety and Security in African Universities

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Association of African Universities (AAU) is pleased to invite stakeholders to a strategic workshop on Safety and Security being hosted under the theme “Revival and Refocusing of Security Departments in African Universities and Colleges in the 21st Century.” This event forms part of the AAU’s ongoing commitment to enhancing safety and security and promoting a peaceful environment to advance excellence in higher education across Africa. The workshop will take place from March 18-20, 2025, at the Pearle Beach Resort, Mauritius, and is being hosted in collaboration with the University of Technology, Mauritius. To register to participate, please click on this link – https://forms.office.com/r/HjqAUhTzcX.

This initiative aligns with AAU’s mission to strengthen the capacity of leaders within Africa’s higher education community. Safety and security are critical issues facing African universities, as many campuses grapple with violent protests, gender-based violence, theft, and other criminal activities (Dlamini & Olarewaju, 2021; Mkhize et al., 2022). For instance, movements like FeesMustFall in South Africa and incidents of sexual violence on various campuses have highlighted the urgent need for effective security policies and measures.

Research indicates that integrating safety and security measures can significantly reduce risks, enhance resilience, and improve overall campus life (Gallagher Content Team, 2024). Secure campuses foster positive learning environments, boost academic outcomes, encourage community engagement, and enhance institutional reputations. This workshop seeks to address these challenges by equipping institutions with the tools and strategies needed to safeguard students, staff, and assets effectively.

OBJECTIVES

The workshop aims to provide a vital platform for enhancing campus safety and security across African universities.

Specifically, the workshop seeks to:

Enhance the knowledge and skills of security personnel, enabling them to design and implement advanced access control systems, effectively leveraging cutting-edge technology.

Emphasize the importance of adopting proactive security policies, including regular safety audits, emergency preparedness drills, and clear communication channels for incident reporting

Promote a collaborative approach involving students, faculty, and administration to foster a safer campus environment.

Cover essential topics such as personal safety and awareness, emergency response and evacuation procedures, cybersecurity and data protection, conflict resolution and de-escalation techniques, first aid and CPR training, and asset-cycle management.

WORKSHOP STRUCTURE

Each course is designed as a module delivered through an intensive 3-day session. Key topics will include:

Personal Safety and Awareness

Emergency Response and Evacuation Procedures

Cybersecurity and Data Protection

Conflict Resolution and De-escalation Techniques

First Aid and CPR Training

Asset life-cycle management

METHODOLOGY

The workshop has adopted a strategic methodology that will include effective approaches, such as the use of case studies, focused group discussions, experiential learning (case studies from universities in the various regions of Africa), presentations, and sharing of ideas, knowledge, and skills. The workshop will institute a follow-up process to ensure that university management implements the good practices to be learned from the workshop at their various institutions of higher learning. Participants will have the opportunity to engage in dialogue with peers on the various challenges at their universities and strategies to overcome them. A postworkshop report will be compiled, and recommendations made will be integrated into improving subsequent workshops.

TARGET GROUP

The workshop is designed for key decision-makers and stakeholders, including

Vice Chancellors, Presidents, Rectors, Directors, Registrars, Campus Security and Safety Officers, and other Professionals responsible for formulating and implementing security policies.

Applications are open for the International Union for the Scientific Study of Population (IUSSP) Early Career Award 2027. The IUSSP Early Career Award was established by the IUSSP Council in 2023. The Award aims to acknowledge and honor outstanding contributions to the development of the discipline and the broad field of population studies by early career scholars in different world regions and boost the global visibility of their achievements.

The IUSSP Early Career Award is offered in the following world regions: Africa, Asia and the Pacific, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and North America. One award will be bestowed per region in a unique collaboration with the Union for African Population Studies (UAPS), the Asian Population Association (APA), the European Association for Population Studies (EAPS), the Latin American Population Association (ALAP), and the Population Association of America (PAA). The Awards will be bestowed every other year; the next set of awards will be announced in 2027.

Benefits

The Awardees will be given an opportunity to present their current work and research interests in an 2027 Early Career Awards webinar and will be entitled to a Free Registration for the next International Population Conference of the IUSSP (IPC 2029, in Barcelona, Spain), where they will be presented in an Awards ceremony.

Eligibility

Candidates should be early career scholars in the population field with not more than 7 years of experience after their PhD at the time of nomination (after 1 November 2019). [*Extension of the eligibility period for up to 3 years may be accepted to account for career interruptions such as maternity/paternity leave, child/elderly-care, or illness; these career interruptions should be listed in the (self-)nomination letter.]

Candidates from a region should be residents of that region at the time of nomination; in case of temporary postings (e.g. as a postdoc) candidates will qualify for the award from the region in which they are permanently/mainly based.

a 1-2 page explanatory statement/letter of nomination that can also include supporting statements from sponsors

any justifications for leaves of absence for those who received their PhD more than 7 years ago

TITLE: United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship 2027: 9-Month Leadership Programme for Social Entrepreneurs and Leaders

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship 2027 is inviting ambitious social entrepreneurs and leaders across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to apply for a nine-month leadership development programme designed for individuals who are building and scaling solutions to poverty and social inequality.

The Fellowship is intended for leaders who have already built an organisation, initiative or social enterprise that is demonstrating meaningful impact and who are ready to strengthen their leadership, expand their organisation’s reach and address the wider systems connected to the problems they are tackling.

Applications for the 2027 UK Acumen Fellowship are open from 22 September to 3 November 2026, with applications closing on 3 November 2026. Successful applicants will participate in a programme running from February to October 2027.

What Is the United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship?

The United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship is a leadership programme offered through Acumen Academy for social entrepreneurs and leaders working to address poverty, inequality and other pressing social challenges.

Acumen Academy describes its community as one for ambitious builders who use “moral imagination” to solve problems of poverty. The Academy works with founders, CEOs and senior leaders by helping them develop both the practical skills required to scale organisations and the leadership capabilities needed to contribute to a more equitable society.

The UK Fellowship specifically brings together leaders from England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland who have demonstrated that their organisations or initiatives are already creating meaningful impact.

Rather than being designed for individuals who are only beginning to explore an idea, the Fellowship is aimed at people who have already built something that works and who are now looking to take their impact further.

Participants will spend nine months learning alongside a cohort of peers from different locations, sectors, backgrounds and areas of social impact. The programme focuses on strengthening leadership, deepening organisational impact and understanding the systemic challenges that influence the problems participants are working to solve.

Who Is the United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship For?

The Fellowship is designed for social entrepreneurs and leaders who are already creating measurable or demonstrated social impact.

Applicants should generally be individuals who:

Lead an organisation, social enterprise or initiative that is already operating.

Have demonstrated meaningful impact through their work.

Have a credible vision for expanding their impact.

Are working on issues connected to poverty, inequality, opportunity or related social challenges.

Want to strengthen their leadership capabilities as their organisation grows.

Are interested in addressing the systems and structural issues underlying the problems they are tackling.

Are prepared to learn alongside and contribute to a diverse cohort of other leaders.

The programme recognises that as organisations grow, leadership challenges can become increasingly complex. Leaders may face difficult decisions about growth, values, organisational priorities, partnerships, capital and how to maintain their original purpose while reaching more people.

The Fellowship therefore focuses not only on organisational growth but also on the leadership required to navigate that growth responsibly.

Why Leadership Matters in Scaling Social Impact

According to Acumen Academy, growing an organisation is not simply about having a successful model. As impact increases, leaders may encounter increasingly difficult and complex decisions.

Growth can create pressure to change the elements that originally made an organisation successful. Leaders may also find themselves measuring success using indicators that do not necessarily reflect the purpose that motivated the organisation in the first place.

The Acumen Fellowship is designed to help leaders navigate these challenges by strengthening practices such as:

Maintaining organisational values while managing growth.

Communicating a compelling vision to partners and potential sources of capital.

Navigating uncertainty and complexity.

Managing competing priorities and tensions.

Building collective action.

Developing a clear understanding of what success means for their organisation.

Remaining connected to the people and communities their work is intended to serve.

The programme refers to this approach as moral leadership, viewing leadership as a practical set of behaviours and decisions that can influence collective action and determine whether an organisation grows in alignment with its underlying purpose.

Key Areas of Social Impact

The UK Acumen Fellowship welcomes leaders working across a range of social challenges.

The programme highlights areas including:

Education

Employment

Healthcare

Food systems

Livelihoods

Opportunity and economic inclusion

Poverty reduction

Social inequality

Community development

Other areas where entrepreneurial solutions can expand opportunities and improve people’s lives

The Fellowship is particularly relevant to leaders whose work provides people experiencing poverty with greater choice, opportunity and dignity through employment, education, products, services or other entrepreneurial solutions.

What Makes an Acumen Fellow?

Acumen Academy identifies several characteristics associated with the leaders it seeks for the Fellowship.

1. You Have Built Something That Works

Applicants should already be leading an organisation or initiative that is delivering real and demonstrated impact.

This means the Fellowship is intended for leaders beyond the earliest idea-development stage. Applicants should be able to demonstrate that their work is functioning in practice and producing meaningful results.

The organisation or initiative should also have a credible vision for reaching more people and influencing the systems connected to the issue being addressed.

2. You Are Committed to Dignity and Opportunity

Acumen places significant emphasis on the belief that the opposite of poverty is dignity.

The Fellowship seeks leaders whose work gives people living in poverty greater dignity and choice through opportunities such as jobs, education, products and services.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate how their work contributes to expanding opportunities and improving people’s lives.

3. You Are Thinking Beyond Incremental Growth

The Fellowship is designed for leaders who want to significantly expand their impact rather than simply make small improvements.

Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate ambition for the future of their organisation or initiative and a desire to understand how their work can contribute to broader systemic change.

The programme is therefore relevant to leaders who are asking questions such as how they can reach more people, influence wider systems and strengthen the long-term sustainability of their work.

4. You Are Ready to Grow as a Leader

The programme recognises that organisational growth can test leaders in new ways.

Applicants should be willing to examine their own leadership approaches, learn from others and engage with peers who can challenge and support them.

The Fellowship places value on accountability, reflection, collaboration and learning within a cohort.

What Does the Acumen Fellowship Programme Include?

The Fellowship lasts nine months and combines several forms of learning and engagement.

Participants continue running their organisations while taking part in a programme structured around the realities of a leader’s working schedule.

The programme combines:

In-person immersive learning.

Virtual workshops.

Self-paced learning.

Group calls.

Assignments.

Peer learning and accountability.

Leadership development.

Opportunities to reflect on organisational growth and systemic challenges.

The hybrid structure is designed to enable participants to develop their leadership without stepping away from their organisations for the duration of the programme.

Three Four-Day In-Person Immersives

The programme includes three four-day, full-time in-person immersives held at different locations in the United Kingdom.

These immersive sessions provide participants with opportunities to engage deeply with the curriculum and their peers.

Each immersive also involves approximately four hours of assignments.

Importantly, UK Acumen Academy covers programme costs for the in-person immersives, including lodging and food.

Two Five-Week Virtual Workshop Series

The Fellowship also includes two five-week virtual workshop series.

Participants can expect approximately four hours of assignments each week, consisting of:

Self-paced learning.

Facilitated sessions.

Group calls.

This structure allows Fellows to integrate the learning into their ongoing professional responsibilities while continuing to lead their organisations.

Acumen Fellowship Curriculum

The curriculum is designed to help social entrepreneurs strengthen the leadership capabilities required to navigate growth, complexity and systemic challenges.

Among the areas covered are Polarity Management, Good Society Readings, Adaptive Leadership and Authentic Voice.

Polarity Management

Leadership frequently involves balancing competing or seemingly contradictory needs.

The Fellowship uses Polarity Management as a practice for helping leaders understand tensions, navigate trade-offs and identify ways forward toward shared objectives.

This can be particularly relevant for social entrepreneurs who must balance issues such as organisational growth and mission, financial sustainability and social impact, or individual organisational needs and broader systemic objectives.

Good Society Readings

The programme also encourages Fellows to step back from day-to-day organisational growth and consider the broader question of what they are building toward.

The Good Society Readings draw on thinkers including Plato, Amartya Sen and Chimamanda Adichie to explore questions concerning a just society and how leaders can ensure that organisational growth remains connected to broader social purpose.

Adaptive Leadership

Social problems rarely have straightforward solutions.

Adaptive Leadership focuses on helping leaders diagnose underlying causes, understand competing perspectives and develop approaches that enable people to work collectively on difficult challenges.

This component can be particularly relevant to social entrepreneurs dealing with complex or deeply rooted social problems where technical solutions alone may not be sufficient.

Authentic Voice

The Fellowship also recognises the importance of communicating a compelling story.

The Authentic Voice component focuses on using values and lived experience to develop narratives that connect with others, build shared purpose and encourage people to take action.

For social entrepreneurs, this can support efforts to communicate organisational purpose to communities, partners, funders and other stakeholders.

Benefits of the United Kingdom Acumen Fellowship

The Fellowship offers participants a combination of leadership development, peer learning, practical support and access to a wider social-impact community.

Key benefits include:

Leadership Development

Fellows receive new leadership frameworks and opportunities to test their developing skills in real-world situations.

The programme is designed to help leaders become more reflective, adaptive and capable of navigating the challenges associated with organisational growth.

Peer Community

Participants join a cohort of leaders working across different issues, locations and backgrounds.

This creates opportunities to exchange experiences, challenge assumptions, learn from other social entrepreneurs and build relationships with people facing similar leadership challenges.

Organisational Impact

The Fellowship is intended to help leaders deepen their organisation’s impact while considering the systemic challenges underlying their work.

Participants can use the learning to examine their organisational models, leadership practices and approaches to scaling.

Long-Term Acumen Community

The relationship with Acumen does not necessarily end when the nine-month Fellowship finishes.

Upon completing the Fellows Programme, participants join the Foundry, Acumen’s global community of more than 2,000 social innovators across 71 countries. The community’s work has reached more than 50 million people, according to Acumen Academy.

The Foundry provides continued opportunities for:

Tools and coaching

Community

Amplification

A path to capital

These elements are intended to support Fellows beyond the formal nine-month programme.

Examples of Impact from Previous UK Fellows

The Acumen Fellowship highlights several previous UK Fellows whose organisations have developed their reach and capabilities.

Yasmin Khan – Staying Put

Yasmin Khan, CEO of Staying Put, works to transform the lives of people experiencing domestic abuse and sexual violence.

According to Acumen Academy, since beginning the Fellowship in 2020, Staying Put has nearly doubled its revenue and team and expanded its reach from approximately 10,000 to more than 18,000 people.

Marcellus Baz – Switch Up

Marcellus Baz, Founder and CEO of Switch Up, works to create pathways for criminalised young people to break the cycle of reoffending.

Acumen Academy reports that since beginning the Fellowship in 2020, Switch Up has more than doubled its revenue and team, expanded its reach from 600 to 1,300 young people, and launched Uniting Nottz, a regional cross-sector partnership.

Michelle Hill – TLC: Talk, Listen, Change

Michelle Hill, CEO of TLC: Talk, Listen, Change, works with individuals and families to rebuild safety, voice and choice.

According to Acumen Academy, opportunities connected to the Fellowship helped TLC secure £260,000 in social investment from Postcode Innovation Trust and pro bono support from Bain & Company during an important organisational challenge.

Hill has also trained as an Acumen facilitator and contributed to UK and global Fellowship sessions.

These examples illustrate the types of organisational growth, leadership development and wider opportunities associated with the Acumen community, while individual outcomes will naturally vary among Fellows.

How Applicants Can Prepare

Although the Fellowship is intended for experienced social entrepreneurs and leaders, applicants can strengthen their preparation by clearly communicating the substance and impact of their work.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate:

What problem the organisation or initiative is addressing.

Who benefits from the work.

What the organisation has already achieved.

Evidence of meaningful impact.

The applicant’s role in leading the organisation.

The organisation’s future ambitions.

Why participation in a leadership-focused Fellowship is relevant at this stage of the applicant’s journey.

Applicants should focus on demonstrating the substance of their work and leadership experience rather than simply describing their ambitions.

Why the Fellowship May Be Relevant to Social Entrepreneurs

Social entrepreneurs often have to manage several competing demands simultaneously.

They may be responsible for organisational strategy, fundraising, partnerships, team development, community engagement, financial sustainability and social impact. As an organisation grows, these responsibilities can become increasingly complex.

The Acumen Fellowship is structured around this reality.

Its curriculum combines leadership frameworks, reflective learning, peer relationships and practical application. Participants continue running their organisations while applying lessons from the Fellowship to real-world leadership challenges.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to established social entrepreneurs who have moved beyond simply developing an idea and are now confronting the challenges of scaling an organisation or expanding its impact.

Research Priorities

Emotional development and well-being: Research on emotion regulation, resilience, identity, agency, self-esteem, and social connection.

Social development and relationships: Research on friendships, family relationships, belonging, communication, empathy, social skills, and the relationship between AI and human connection.

Patterns, contexts, and variance across demographics: Research on how outcomes vary by time spent, type and purpose of use, age, culture, language, socioeconomic circumstances, and other individual or contextual factors.

Proposals will be evaluated based on:

Scientific rigor: The strength and appropriateness of the research design and analysis

Relevance: Examination of a topic relevant to current public discourse on AI

Proposal quality: The clarity, focus, and coherence of the application

Ethics and safeguarding: The adequacy of protections for minors and other participants

Feasibility: Whether the project can be completed with the proposed resources and timeline

Team expertise: The team’s ability to conduct the proposed work responsibly

Inclusion and generalizability: Attention to diverse populations, contexts, cultures, and experiences

TITLE: How a youth led start up is transforming learning using Educational Technology and Innovative Education Delivery Approaches

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
One key strategy taken by most governments around the world, to contain the spread of the coronavirus disease was to close educational institutions. These closures have affected millions of learners not only in Africa, but globally.

In their bid to keep learning ongoing, most institutions have had to turn to online methods of teaching and learning. This has heightened the need to adopt innovative education delivery approaches, as well as increased demand for the support of educational technology learning experts.

Edutab.africa, is one such organisation which has been working closely with institutions in Africa to improve teaching and learning using technology and other engaging and innovative learning approaches. It is a youth led organisation created by a group of four young men in Kenya in 2018 to promote Educational Technology and other engaging learning approaches. The founders are from different training backgrounds ranging from Mathematics, Education, Development studies and Computing. One key objective of Edutab.africa is how to use educational technology to close the learning gap as well as increase collaboration and student engagement. Virtual learning environments in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts & Mathematics) areas has also been one of their key areas of focus.

The COVID-19 crisis presented an opportunity to expedite some of their programs in Kenya and increase their efforts to promote Educational Technology in Africa and beyond.

The following are some of the projects that Edutab.africa has been engaged in.

Supporting the Association of African Universities’ e-Learning Training for One of its member institutions

In line with supporting African Higher Education Institutions to quickly move their teaching and learning online, the AAU ran a pilot training on e-Learning for 170 academic staff from the Lupane State University, Zimbabwe. Three of Edutab.africa’s team members – Michael Mumbo, Maxwell Fundi and Patrick Njoroge were among the team of over 90 e-Learning volunteers from across the world who worked with the AAU to deliver the virtual training as support facilitators and mentors on the use of Moodle for learning and teaching between May and July 2020.

Robotics & Programming

Prior to the outbreak of the COVID 19 pandemic, Edutab.africa had been running face-to-face programming, robotics and extracurricular math activities for students in STEM clubs in both primary and secondary schools. With the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, the dynamics of teaching and learning has changed significantly. Edutab.africa now run their sessions virtually. This has opened an avenue for students across the globe (not only those from Kenya) to participate in these programming sessions.

Implementing Kolibri for Low Resourced Schools

Through collaboration with Learning Equality, Edutab.africa has been implementing an Educational Technology project that uses Kolibri, an open source offline content management software to deliver OER materials to schools and communities in low resource settings across Kenya. This has been achieved through the use of low-cost computing – Raspberry-Pis as offline content servers for educational content used via a local network with tablets, phones and computers.

International Community for Collaborative Content Creation (IC4) Project

As part of promoting global cooperation, Edutab.africa has been involved in the International Community for Collaborative Content Creation (IC4) Project, a project bringing students from different continents to participate in collaborative STEAM Activities. In this project which started in 2016, students drawn from different socioeconomic backgrounds in Kenya, Finland, USA, Cameroon, Namibia and Brazil were introduced to participatory teaching through a network of Media Making Clubs (MMC). These MMCs, connected via internet and other technologies, have been making digital artefacts (including videos, short subject films, games, computer programs, and specialized applications) that represent, explain and clarify STEAM. The main aim of this project is to foster meaningful and scientifically rigorous collaborations that cross and connect cultures in STEAM areas.

TITLE: How Nurses Can Plan the Next Step in Their Career

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Many nurses eventually reach a point where they wonder what comes next. After building experience, it is natural to want growth, a stronger voice, or a larger role in improving patient care. Some nurses want to lead teams, mentor newer colleagues, teach, shape policy, or expand their clinical authority. The next step does not have to feel uncertain. With thoughtful planning, nurses can choose a path that fits their goals, schedules, and responsibilities.

Why Advance Now

Healthcare is changing quickly, and nurses are needed in broader, more influential roles across hospitals, clinics, and community settings. Employers increasingly value professionals who can lead teams, improve systems, solve complex problems, and advocate for better outcomes. That demand is one reason many working nurses explore online MSN to DNP programs. For nurses who want to keep working while continuing their education, these programs can offer a practical path.

Advancing now can also prepare nurses for future opportunities before they become urgent. Leadership and advanced practice roles bring greater responsibility, but they also allow nurses to help shape decisions instead of only responding to them. In these positions, nurses may mentor colleagues, improve workflows, and influence patient outcomes on a wider scale.

Career growth is not only about earning a new title or degree. It is also about expanding your voice, increasing your impact, and building a future in which your experience can influence healthcare more broadly.

Career Goals First

Before choosing a program, nurses should define what they truly want. The next career step should reflect personal interests, strengths, and long-term goals, not just what sounds impressive or what others suggest. Some nurses are drawn to leadership roles where they can oversee staff, improve department operations, and guide teams through change. Others want stronger clinical authority so they can play a larger role in patient care decisions.

Teaching is another common goal. That may mean working with nursing students, leading staff development, or training teams within a healthcare system. Other nurses are interested in policy, quality improvement, or organizational change and want to influence care beyond the bedside. Financial advancement can also be part of the decision, and that is a valid reason to consider further education.

A useful first step is to write down your top three career goals. Specific goals make it easier to evaluate options. Once goals are defined, it becomes much easier to identify the degree or program that supports them.

Fit School Into Life

For many nurses, the biggest challenge is not motivation but time. Long shifts, family commitments, charting, and everyday responsibilities can make school seem difficult to manage. Still, many nurses succeed because they build a plan around real life rather than waiting for a perfect moment.

Start by looking honestly at your weekly routine. Identify where studying can happen consistently, whether that means a few evenings a week, early mornings, or a block of time on weekends. Small, regular study sessions are often more realistic and effective than trying to do everything at once.

It also helps to talk with the people in your household before classes begin. Setting expectations about study time, shared responsibilities, and support during busy periods can reduce tension later. If you have children, childcare planning is especially important. Choosing a program format that fits your life from the beginning can make a major difference in stress and your ability to stay on track.

The goal is not perfect balance. The goal is a routine that remains workable even when work is busy and life becomes unpredictable.

What to Compare

When researching programs, it is easy to focus on polished websites and broad promises. What matters most are the details that will shape your day-to-day experience. Flexibility should be one of the first things you examine. Consider whether classes are asynchronous, live online, or a mix of both, and think about how each option will fit around your shifts.

Support services are just as important as scheduling. Look for strong academic advising, responsive faculty, technical support, and writing assistance. If a program says it is designed for working professionals, there should be clear evidence that this support exists in practice.

Clinical requirements are another major factor. Make sure you understand how placements are handled, how many hours are required, and how much responsibility falls on you to arrange them. Also compare expected time to completion, total tuition, and overall program reputation.

A faster path is not always the best choice if the pace will leave you exhausted. A lower-cost program is not always the best value if weak support makes delays more likely. Read carefully, ask direct questions, and pay attention when answers are vague.

Costs and Planning

Paying for school can feel overwhelming, but it becomes more manageable when costs are broken into categories. Start by looking at the total expense, not just tuition. Include fees, books, technology needs, travel for any in-person requirements, and possible clinical costs.

Next, ask whether your employer offers tuition reimbursement or education assistance. Many healthcare organizations support continuing education, especially when it helps build leadership and advanced practice capacity. Scholarships and grants are also worth exploring, even if they seem competitive.

Creating a simple budget can make planning easier. Review your monthly income, fixed expenses, and how much flexibility you have for education costs. Some nurses choose to save for several months before enrolling so they have a financial cushion. Planning ahead may not remove every challenge, but it can reduce stress and help you move forward with greater confidence.

Skills That Matter

Advanced education is not just about adding credentials to a resume. It also develops skills that are highly valuable in real healthcare settings. Communication is one of the most important. Nurses moving into larger roles need to explain ideas clearly, lead conversations, advocate effectively, and handle difficult discussions professionally.

Leadership skills also become more practical. Nurses learn how to guide change, support teams, and make decisions in situations where the answers are not simple. That kind of judgment is essential in healthcare, where competing priorities and complex patient needs are common.

Decision-making and systems thinking are especially important. Instead of focusing on one patient situation at a time, nurses begin to see how staffing, workflow, communication, and policy affect outcomes across an entire unit or organization. This broader perspective can make a nurse more effective in both clinical and administrative roles.

TITLE: 8.582 Selected Topics in Condensed Matter Physics

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
8.582 Selected Topics in Condensed Matter Physics

by Xiao-Gang Wen

2026 Spring, 2:30 PM to 4:00 PM on Wednesday and Friday in Room 56-154, MIT

Course site: https://canvas.mit.edu/courses/37294

Artificial intelligence is based on neural networks. A well-trained neural network develops an intricate internal structure that enables remarkable capabilities. However, describing and characterizing this internal structure remains a difficult and largely open challenge.

A similar problem arises in many-body physics. Many-body systems can be described using tensor networks. Under renormalization via coarse graining, a tensor network flows toward a fixed point. The fixed-point tensor network possesses rich internal structures that characterize gapped and gapless phases, emergent symmetries, emergent gauge interactions, as well as emergent Fermi and fractional statistics, etc. A central question is how to uncover and understand the intricate structures hidden in these fixed-point tensor networks.

The first part of this course introduces the tensor network approach to many-body systems. We will discuss numerical methods for driving the renormalization of tensor networks, and then explain how to extract the algebraic structures encoded in fixed-point tensor networks. Using the tensor network formalism, we will study many-body entanglement, topological order, symmetry-protected topological order, generalized symmetries, and related topics.

1) Discrete path integral (tensor network) for many-body systems.
2) Tensor network renormalization for gapped phases and gapless phase transitions
3) Algebra structures (Frobenius algebra, pentagon equation) in fixed-point tensor network
4) Fixed-point tensor network and exactly soluble model
5) Chain, cochain, cycle, cocycle – realization and classification of SPT phases
6) Quantum circuit: short-range entanglement and long-range entanglement
7) Topologically ordered phases
8) Holographic picture of generalized symmetry as topological order in one higher dimension.
9) Emergent generalized symmetry determine critical points.
10) … …

There will be weekly homework, due on Friday (65% of grade).
There will also be a term paper (35% of grade).

TITLE: UN Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme 2026: Belgium-Funded Opportunities in Political Affairs, Humanitarian Affairs and Coordination

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The United Nations Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme offers young professionals an opportunity to gain practical experience working within United Nations organizations, funds, programmes and offices involved in development, humanitarian affairs, policy, coordination and other areas of international cooperation.

In August 2026, Belgium announced three new JPO positions for young professionals seeking experience within the UN system. The available positions are based in New York, East Jerusalem and Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, and cover political affairs, humanitarian affairs and UN coordination.

The current openings are particularly relevant to qualified young professionals interested in international development, multilateral affairs, humanitarian action, UN reform, policy coordination and international cooperation.

Application deadline for all three positions: September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time).

What Is the United Nations JPO Programme?

The United Nations Junior Professional Officer Programme is a professional development initiative designed to give young experts practical experience within the UN system.

JPOs work within participating UN organizations, funds, programmes and offices that finance, support or implement development and other international programmes.

The programme is designed to combine professional experience, training and exposure to the work of the United Nations.

A JPO is not simply placed in an administrative position. Depending on the assignment, the officer can contribute to activities such as:

Programme development

Policy analysis

Programme formulation

Programme implementation

Monitoring

Evaluation

Coordination

Research

Strategic planning

Humanitarian affairs

Political affairs

International development

Multilateral cooperation

JPOs receive guidance and training from senior UN staff and participate in the work of their assigned organization.

This makes the programme particularly valuable for young professionals who want to build a long-term career in the United Nations, international development, humanitarian affairs, diplomacy, public policy or multilateral organizations.

Belgium-Funded UN JPO Opportunities Open in 2026

The latest Belgian call includes three specific JPO assignments.

These are:

JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform

JPO in Humanitarian Affairs

JPO in Coordination

Although all three positions fall under the broader JPO Programme, they have different responsibilities, locations and institutional environments.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the individual vacancy notice before applying.

1. JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform

The first opening is a JPO position in Political Affairs focused on supporting UN reform.

Duty station

United Nations Executive Office of the Secretary-General (EOSG)

Office of the Under-Secretary-General for Policy, UN80 Secretariat

New York, United States

The position provides an opportunity for a young professional to work in an environment connected to high-level UN policy and reform processes.

The role is particularly relevant to candidates interested in:

International affairs

Political affairs

UN reform

Multilateral diplomacy

International policy

Strategic analysis

United Nations systems

Global governance

Public policy

Institutional reform

Application deadline

September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time).

The second opening is a JPO position in Humanitarian Affairs.

East Jerusalem

This position offers exposure to the work of OCHA and the coordination of humanitarian affairs.

It may be particularly relevant to professionals interested in:

Humanitarian affairs

Humanitarian coordination

Humanitarian policy

International organizations

Humanitarian operations

3. JPO in Coordination

Duty station

United Nations Resident Coordinator System (RCS)

Resident Coordinator Office (RCO)

Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire

The Resident Coordinator System plays an important role in bringing different parts of the UN development system together at country level.

This opportunity may therefore be particularly relevant to candidates interested in:

UN coordination

Development coordination

International development

Programme management

Policy coordination

Partnerships

Multilateral cooperation

Development programmes

UN country teams

Strategic planning

Application deadline

September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time).

Click HERE to read more and apply.

How the Belgian JPO Programme Works

The Belgian JPO Programme is connected to Belgian Development Cooperation and provides young professionals with an opportunity to work within participating UN organizations.

According to the programme information, JPO assignments are based either:

In one of Belgium’s partner countries for development cooperation;

At the regional level; or

At the headquarters of a participating UN organization.

The design of JPO positions takes into account the strategic priorities of Belgian Development Cooperation.

JPOs are also expected to receive professional training and supervision from senior staff.

What Does a JPO Actually Do?

A Junior Professional Officer can become involved in different stages of programme and policy work.

The programme description specifically indicates that JPOs may participate in:

Programme definition

JPOs can contribute to identifying priorities and helping define programmes and interventions.

Programme formulation

They can support the development and formulation of programmes, projects and policy initiatives.

Programme implementation

JPOs can participate in putting programmes into practice and supporting implementation activities.

Monitoring

They can contribute to monitoring progress, outputs, activities and results.

Evaluation

JPOs may also participate in assessing whether programmes and interventions are achieving their intended objectives.

This combination gives participants exposure to the full programme cycle, rather than limiting them to one isolated area of work.

Why the UN JPO Programme Is a Valuable Career Opportunity

For young professionals interested in international development and multilateral organizations, a JPO assignment can provide valuable professional exposure.

1. Gain UN System Experience

Working directly within a UN organization or office can provide practical experience that is difficult to obtain through academic study alone.

Participants can gain insight into:

UN procedures

Multilateral coordination

International development programmes

Policy processes

Programme management

Institutional decision-making

International cooperation

2. Work Alongside Experienced UN Professionals

JPOs receive training and professional support from senior staff.

This provides an opportunity to learn from experienced professionals working on international policy and development issues.

3. Develop Programme Management Skills

Because JPOs can participate in programme formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, the programme can help participants develop practical skills across the project cycle.

These skills are transferable to careers in:

UN agencies

International NGOs

Development organizations

Government institutions

Multilateral organizations

Research organizations

Consulting

Public policy

4. Build International Professional Networks

Working in a UN environment can allow young professionals to interact with colleagues from different countries, professional backgrounds and UN entities.

Building these professional relationships can be valuable for future international career opportunities.

5. Gain Exposure to International Policy

Depending on the assignment, JPOs may work on major global issues including:

Political affairs

Humanitarian response

Development

UN reform

Coordination

Gender equality

Public policy

Human rights

Health

Food security

Migration

Environmental issues

The specific experience will depend on the JPO position.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The programme is particularly relevant to young experts and early-career professionals who want to build experience in international organizations.

Potentially relevant backgrounds can include:

International relations

Political science

International development

Public policy

Economics

Law

Public administration

Humanitarian studies

Development studies

Social sciences

Programme management

International cooperation

Other fields relevant to the specific JPO position

However, the exact educational qualifications, professional experience, nationality requirements and other eligibility conditions can differ by JPO vacancy.

Applicants should therefore not assume that meeting the general JPO description automatically makes them eligible for every position.

The individual vacancy notice should be checked carefully.

What Qualifications Are Important?

While the exact requirements differ between positions, competitive candidates should generally expect to demonstrate a combination of:

Academic background

A relevant university degree or equivalent academic qualification appropriate to the assignment.

Relevant professional experience

Experience related to the substantive area of the JPO position can strengthen an application.

For example:

Political affairs experience for a political affairs position

Humanitarian experience for a humanitarian affairs position

Programme or development coordination experience for a coordination position

Analytical skills

UN positions frequently require the ability to analyze information, prepare documents and contribute to evidence-based decision-making.

Communication skills

Strong written and verbal communication is important in an international organization.

International or development exposure

Experience working with development programmes, NGOs, governments, international organizations or related institutions can be relevant.

Again, these are general indicators, not a substitute for the formal eligibility criteria contained in each vacancy announcement.

How to Choose Between the Three Current JPO Positions

Applicants should select the position that best matches their professional background and career objectives.

Choose Political Affairs – UN Reform if you are interested in:

UN reform

International politics

Global governance

Policy analysis

Multilateral affairs

Strategic policy

Choose Humanitarian Affairs – OCHA if you are interested in:

Humanitarian response

Emergency affairs

Humanitarian coordination

Advocacy

Crisis response

International humanitarian work

Choose Coordination – RCS if you are interested in:

UN development coordination

Programme management

Development policy

Partnerships

UN country-team coordination

International development

The best application is not necessarily the position with the most prestigious-sounding title. It is the position where your education, experience, skills and career goals align most strongly with the job description.

Application Deadline

All three currently advertised Belgian-funded JPO positions have the same application deadline:

September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time).

Applicants should make sure they understand the deadline in their own time zone and submit before the closing time rather than waiting until the final day.

How to Apply

The application process is vacancy-specific.

Applicants should:

Step 1: Identify the position that matches your profile

Review the three available assignments and determine which one most closely corresponds to your qualifications and career goals.

Step 2: Read the complete vacancy notice

Do not rely only on the general JPO programme description.

Read the specific PDF for:

Required qualifications

Required experience

Nationality requirements

Language requirements

Responsibilities

Duty station

Application procedure

Supporting documents

Deadline

Step 3: Prepare your application

Ensure your CV and supporting materials clearly demonstrate how your experience matches the requirements of the position.

Step 4: Highlight relevant experience

Focus your application on evidence that demonstrates your ability to contribute to the specific assignment.

Step 5: Submit before the deadline

Applications must be submitted no later than September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time).

Conclusion

The Belgian-funded United Nations Junior Professional Officer Programme provides young professionals with an opportunity to gain practical experience within the UN system while contributing to international policy, humanitarian affairs, development and coordination work.

The three current openings provide different career pathways: Political Affairs and UN Reform in New York, Humanitarian Affairs with OCHA in East Jerusalem, and Coordination with the UN Resident Coordinator System in Abidjan.

For the three positions currently advertised, the critical deadline is September 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time). Candidates should review the complete official vacancy notice for their preferred position and prepare a highly targeted application that clearly demonstrates their suitability for the assignment.

TITLE: Ashoka Carnegie Challenge for Civic Leadership 2027 (Seed Grants for Changemakers & more)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Deadline: January 31, 2027

The Carnegie Challenge for Civic Leadership 2027 is now open! Do you have an idea for creating positive change in your school or community? Or are you already working on a project for good and engaging others to make a difference? That’s civic leadership: identifying a challenge in your community and working with others to create solutions, inspire action, and make a positive difference.

Ashoka Changemakers is calling on everyone aged 20 and under living in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, the United States, and U.S. territories. Are you leading a project that’s making a difference? Are you part of a youth-led organization that helps people get involved in their communities? Or do you have an idea to change the world that you’d love to put into action?

If your answer is YES to any of these questions, apply to the Carnegie Challenge for Civic Leadership! This is your chance to win seed funding, connect with other young changemakers, and attend an unforgettable in-person convening.

Benefits

All Eligible Participants Will Receive:

Multiple pathways to funding, with opportunities for early applicants as well as finalists and Grand Prize winners.

Peer feedback via the Challenge online platform, including the opportunity to connect with other Challenge applicants and review applications from peers.

Access to on-demand trainings to support your changemaking journey, plus live support sessions and office hours.

The opportunity to become a certified Ashoka Youth Venturer, whether or not they are selected as a winner of the Challenge. If you’ve taken action on an idea that creates positive change in your school or community, you may be eligible to earn a Youth Venture Certificate from Ashoka, a global leader in youth social entrepreneurship. If you’re not quite ready to be certified yet, Ashoka will work with you to meet the certification criteria. Along the way, you’ll gain access to tools, resources, and a growing community of young changemakers who are leading change together.

Early Application Deadline | Seed Grants: Apply early for the opportunity to receive seed funding to jumpstart your civic leadership journey. Eligible applicants who submit by the Early Application Deadline may be selected to receive a Seed Grant:

United States: Up to 600 applicants who apply by November 17 will be eligible to receive a $100 USD Civic Seed Grant.

Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa: 25 eligible applicants from each country who apply by October 10 will receive a $50 USD Civic Seed Grant.

These grants are designed to help young changemakers take the next step in bringing their ideas to life while continuing through the Challenge.

Finalist Awards: Following the review process, finalists will receive funding to grow their impact.

United States

12 Winners will receive $500 USD Civic Promise Award

10 Finalists will each receive $1,000 USD Civic Impact Award

2 Grand Prize Winners will each receive $10,000 USD Civic Leadership Award

Anyone receiving a grant $500 or above will be considered for a spot at an in-person convening in the US during the week of July 12, 2027 where they will connect, build skills, and celebrate their work alongside fellow young civic leaders. A total of 10 Challenge Winners will be invited to attend the in-person convening.*

*Ashoka will cover eligible travel and participation costs, including airfare, hotel accommodations, ground transportation, and meals during the convening. Chaperone travel will also be provided for eligible participants under 18, in accordance with the Challenge Rules.

Kenya, Nigeria & South Africa

Distributed equally among the three countries, a total of 66 winners will be selected:

30 Winners will each receive $250 USD Civic Promise Award

30 Finalists will each receive $1,000 USD Civic Impact Award

6 Grand Prize Winners will each receive $5,000 USD Civic Leadership Award

Anyone receiving a grant $250 or above will be considered for a spot at an in-person convening during the week of July 26, 2027, where they will connect, build skills, and celebrate their work alongside fellow young civic leaders. *Ashoka will cover eligible travel and participation costs, including airfare, hotel accommodations, ground transportation, and meals during the convening. Chaperone travel will also be provided for eligible participants under 18, in accordance with the Challenge Rules.

Participants must be individuals aged 20 or younger by the end of the entry period (January 31, 2027). Please note: Applicants based in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa who are 17 years old or younger must have an adult support with completing their application. In the United States, applicants who are 12 years old or younger must have an adult support with completing their application.

Participants must be located in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, and/or the United States and U.S. Territories.

Applications must be submitted in English.

The submitted project must be youth-led, with the primary project lead under 20 years of age.
